articleTitle: A Review of Memory Effects in AlGaN/GaN HEMT Based RF PAs
abstract: This work is an overview of the current understanding of memory effects arising from AlGaN/GaN HEMT based RF power amplifiers. It reviews the most widely accepted physical sources of those memory effects and their impact on the amplifier's linearizability, to then discuss corresponding circuit design approaches to minimize the phenomena. This is illustrated by results of a power amplifier whose short-term and long-term nonlinear memory is compensated by an analog assisted digital pre-distortion scheme.

articleTitle: A2–18 GHz 13.5-W Distributed GaN HPA MMIC Based on Stacked and Tapering Techniques
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a 2.0 to 18.0 GHz distributed high-power amplifier (DHPA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) on 150-nm GaN-SiC HEMT process has been presented. By employing 8-cell 2-level-stacked architecture, ultra-wide bandwidth and good power performance are achieved simultaneously. To improve the PAE and gain further, non-uniform distribution, tapering drain-artificial transmission line (D-ATMLs), and inductive gain peaking structures are also incorporated. The proposed HPA MMIC is a fully integrated one with all the necessary components on-chip. Simulated with continuous-wave (CW) excitations, the resulting performance under 35-V VDD power supply shows 18.5 ~ 16.0 dB small-signal gain, 13.5-7.5 W output power, and 38.2-19.5 % power-added efficiency (PAE) over more than 16 GHz frequency band. The die size of the proposed HPA core is around 4.8 × 1.8 mm which is very compact to be implanted into future broadband systems and applications.

articleTitle: A W-band Power Amplifier with 15-dBm Psat and 14% PAE in 0.13-µm SiGe HBT Technology
abstract: In this work, the design of a wideband millimetre-wave (mm-Wave) power amplifier (PA) is presented. To ensure the designed PA has not only a sufficient output power with good power-added efficiency (PAE) but also superior input and output impedance matching, a balanced amplifier (BA) architecture is used. A prototype PA is designed in a 0.13-µm SiGe HBT technology. With a 1.6- V power supply, the PA can deliver more than 15 dBm saturated output power between 85–100 GHz that is equivalent to more than 16% fractional bandwidth. The peak PAE is better than 14.7% within this frequency range. The overall physical dimension of the designed PA is very compact. Including all pads, it is only 0.6 mm x 0.9 mm.

articleTitle: Broadband High Efficiency Quasi-Continuous Class-J Power Amplifier
abstract: In this paper, a broadband high efficiency power amplifier (PA) with quasi-continuous Class-J mode is proposed. Specifically, the continuous current waveform can be obtained within the entire operating frequency band. For lower frequency, its load condition satisfies the requirement of Class-J PA mode. While for the center frequency and higher frequencies, the fundamental termination is more closely to real axis, which extends the bandwidth. Meanwhile, the current dip can be generated by the nonlinear output capacitors, which reshapes the current waveform thus enhancing the efficiency. The proposed PA shows a relatively high performance of greater than 40 dBm saturated output power and delivers an average of 58 % drain efficiency (DE) within the frequency band of 3.5 to 5.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Two-Stage GaAs HBT Doherty Power Amplifier With Thermal Compensation for WLAN Application
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency Doherty power amplifier (DPA) using an InGaP/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) process is presented. The DPA aims for the application of 2.4 GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) systems with a high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). The traditional bulky quarter-wavelength line is realized using a low-pass n-type network for miniaturization and low loss. A thermally compensated dynamic bias circuit is applied to increase thermal stability. Under the excitation of a 40-MHz 64-quadratic-amplitude modu-lation(QAM) signal, the proposed DPA achieves a gain of 29 dB gain, an average power of 26 dBm, and an average power added efficiency (PAE) up to 21%. Good error vector magnitude (EVM) and adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) performance are also measured, which demonstrates EVM and ACLR after digital pre-distortion (DPD) are −42 dB and −50.7 dBc. respectively.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Behavioral Model for GaN HEMTs based on Long-Short Term Memory Networks
abstract: In this paper, a modified recurrent neural network (RNN) technique, long-short term memory (LSTM) algorithm based, small-signal behavioral modeling methodology for Gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) is presented. The verification is carried out on an 8×125 μm GaN HEMT with a 0.25 μm gate feature size. The LSTM model shows excellent modeling performance. The relative error of S-parameters can be controlled under 1%. Compared with exiting support vector regression (SVR) modeling technique, the model extraction time is reduced significantly, while its accuracy is maintained at high level.

articleTitle: Compact 5G N79 Band Pass Filter Based on HR-Silicon IPD Technology
abstract: This paper uses high-resistance silicon-based IPD technology to design a band-pass filter applied to the N79 band of 5G communication. Its operating frequency is 4.4GHz-5GHz, and it uses a hybrid topology of multi-zero low-pass and highpass cascade. The design area of the band-pass filter is 2mm*1.5mm, and the area is compact. Through the analysis of the inductance design and the optimization of the component values, the performance of the passband loss is less than 2dB, the low frequency suppression is greater than 40dB, and the high frequency suppression is greater than 20dB, which has a good selection performance. Finally, the processing and testing of the physical object are completed. The results of the physical test are basically consistent with the simulation, which is suitable for the system-in-package design of the N79-band high-performance RF front-end.

articleTitle: A Two-Chip Cascaded FMCW Radar For 2D Angle Estimation
abstract: Recently, radar sensors with four-dimensional (4D) high resolution are demanded for point cloud processing in automotive radar field. To achieve this goal, a large amount of transmit (TX) and receive (RX) channels are required for radar systems. Commonly, a monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC) chip of an automotive radar has only 3 TX and 4 RX channels. The resolution is restricted by the limited number of transceiver (TRX) channels. Hence, in this paper, a compact and affordable two-chip cascaded frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system is presented. Based on the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology and sparse array method, the proposed module can provide an angular resolution of 3.8° in azimuth and 16° in elevation. In order to demonstrate the designed system performance, further measurement is implemented in microwave anechoic chamber. The measured results show good accordance to the simulations.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Basing on HMSIW Loaded Dual-mode CSRR
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized bandpass filter is proposed basing on half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) loaded dual-mode complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR). The HMSIW is a derivative of substrate integrated waveguide(SIW), and the dimension is 50% of the SIW, so it is more conducive to decrease the size of the filter. Meanwhile, the dual-mode CSRR is loaded on the HMSIW, which can further reduce the size of the filter. Besides, loading dual-mode CSRR can obtain a wider operating bandwidth and generate two transmission zeros in the upper sideband to enhance the frequency selectivity compare with loading traditional CSRR. To verify the validity, the miniaturized bandpass filter is designed and optimized in HFSS software. The simulation results show that the center frequency is 7.44 GHz, 3-dB fractional bandwidth is 16.9% from 6.84 to 8.10 GHz. The final size of the filter is 0.167λg×0.463λg, the miniaturization design of the filter is realized.

articleTitle: A Posture Recognition Based Fall Detection System using a 24GHz CMOS FMCW Radar SoC
abstract: Falls are major cause of accidents in aging population. In this paper, a prototype system of fall-detection based on a CMOS 24G frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar SoC was introduced. In particular, the proposed signal features extracted from Range-Doppler Map are used for detection, while the proposed bi-directional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM), has been used in the classification process. The preliminary classification results are 99.00% for empty-room, walking, standing and falling-down.

articleTitle: Q-band Millimeter Wave Communication: Enabling 10 Gb/s Home Network in Fiber-to- The-Room Scenario
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) technologies have been well studied in both long range outdoor communication and short range indoor communication. Owing to the high propagation loss and blockage of walls, the coverage of mm Wave for indoor scenario is greatly limited. In these two years, with the evolution of the fifth generation fixed network (F5G), the deployment of Fiber-to- The-Room (FTTR) provides a powerful tool to improve the coverage of indoor mmWave communication. Based on the fiber connection between rooms, it is possible to supply extremely high data rate backhaul channels for mmWave communication in every room by FTTR. Furthermore, the large attenuation of walls eliminates the interference between wireless communication systems in different rooms, thus making it possible to build a non-interference home network which significantly outperforms traditional WiFi mesh networks. To verify the performance of Q-band mmWave communication in indoor scenarios, a prototype was designed and data rate higher than 10 Gb/s could be achieved when 4×4 MIMO technology is adopted. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first Q-band communication prototype achieved data rate higher than 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Towards the Exploratory In-Orbit Verification of an E/W-Band Satellite Communication Link
abstract: This contribution details the motivation and the status of a new satellite mission, which targets the in-orbit verification of a wideband satellite communication link operating in the high millimeter-wave regime at 71–76 GHz. The paper reviews the dynamic link budgets for data links between satellites in low-earth orbits and ground stations on close to sea level, taking into account the expected atmospheric attenuation according to lTU models and supported by successful terrestrial transmission experiments, which confirm the feasibility and attractiveness of exploiting allocated spectrum in E-band for Gigabit satellite feeder links of globe-spanning satellite constellations and high capacity data downlinks in earth observation, even under adverse weather conditions. The scientific payload, hosted by a 6V-Cubsat platform, comprises a high-performance E-band transmitter with GaN-based solid state power amplifiers, an InGaAs-based low-noise receiver and a modern FPGA-based digital processing unit realizing AWG functionality and 4k image/video storage. The ground terminal employs a highly directive Cassegrain antenna with coarse GPS and fine RF tracking and a low-noise receiver.

articleTitle: K-band 360° Passive Vector Modulator Phase Shifter with Coupled Line Qadrature Coupler and Passive Transistor Array
abstract: This letter introduces a passive vector modulator phase shifter fabricated by 65-nm CMOS technology. Coupled line quadrature coupler is used to obtain broader bandwidth and more accurate quadrature signals. This work sums up an integrated method to analyze and improve the performance of the passive transistor array, and focuses on the impact of the matching impedance of the transistor array on the circuit performance. The proposed vector modulator phase shifter achieves a phase shift with range of 360° by 5.625° step, and an insertion loss of 11-14dB from 16-26GHz. The minimal RMS of phase error is 1.2° at 21GHz, and the maximum loss difference is 2dB in working frequency.

articleTitle: Ka-band MMIC GaN Doherty Power Amplifiers: Considerations on Technologies and Architectures
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of two sample GaN technologies, one on Silicon and the other on Silicon Carbide substrate, when applied to the design of an integrated Doherty power amplifier. Two different target applications are considered, namely the satellite Ka-band downlink (17.3-20.3 GHz) and terrestrial communications in the n257 FR2 5G band (26.5-29.5 GHz), with different specifications but similar absolute frequency range. Considerations are made highlighting advantages and disadvantages of the two technologies for the design of high frequency MMIC Doherty Power Amplifiers in the presented scenarios.

articleTitle: A 24.2dBm Full W band GaN Power Amplifier with about 40GHz of Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents the development and performance of a gallium nitride (GaN) monolithic millimeter-wave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) covering the full W-band (75-110 GHz). The 4-stage PA, developed using a 100-nm GaN-on-SiC technology, demonstrates a linear gain of more than 15 dB over about 40GHz of bandwidth. Operating in a con-tinuous-wave (CW) mode, it produces a typical output power of 24.2 dBm with power flatness of ± 1 dB over 75-110 GHz. The average power added efficiency is 6.5%. Due to its unique combination of bandwidth, output power and power flatness, this amplifier could be a suitable building block for wideband communication, measurement or phase-arrav systems.

articleTitle: Training of Deep Neural Networks in Electromagnetic Problems: a Case Study of Antenna Array Pattern Synthesis
abstract: This paper discusses the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) for electromagnetic problems. The main concerns include how to modify EM problems to take the advantage of the deep learning techniques and how to tailor conventional deep learning concepts with electromagnetic domain knowledge, which has been overlooked by most existing DNN based EM research. A 1×8 patch antenna array has been adopted as the test vehicle for investigation, with the aim to use deep learning for radiation pattern synthesis. It is analyzed via electromagnetic simulation first to collect sufficient training data sets containing different combinations of excitation signals and corresponding radiation patterns. These data are then pre-processed and passed to DNNs for training to imitate the mapping between excitation signals and radiation patterns. With careful feature selection and DNN architecture optimizations, two DNN models are obtained eventually. One of them aims at forward radiation synthesis in any certain excitation condition, and the other seeks out backward excitation signals needed for a given radiation pattern, and both achieved an accuracy over 80%. This paper may provide enlightenment and reference in applying deep learning to electromagnetic problems in terms of feature selection and architecture modification.

articleTitle: Automatic Modulation Classification Using Fractional Low Order Cyclic Spectrum and Deep Residual Networks in Impulsive Noise
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) plays an important role in cognitive radio, surveillance and electronic warfare systems. However, due to the presence of impulsive noise in wireless communication systems, conventional AMC methods which are based on Gaussian noise assumption usually exhibit poor performance in impulsive noise environment. Aiming at realizing efficient AMC with impulsive noise, a novel AMC method based on fractional low order cyclic spectrum (FLOCS) and deep residual networks (ResNets) is proposed in this paper. In this method, FLOCS can effectively suppress impulsive noise, and meanwhile the discriminating features can also be extracted from FLOCS for AMC. Then, on the basis of these features, deep residual networks are employed to classify different modulation types. Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AMC method can achieve superior classification performance in impulsive noise environment.

articleTitle: Graphene Assembled Film Based Millimeter Wave Antenna Array for 5G Mobile Communications
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave antenna array based on flexible graphene assembled film (GAF) for 5G mobile communications. The GAF has high electrical conductivity of 1.1×106 S/m with thickness of 26 µm and density of 1.45 g/cm3. The proposed GAF antenna array has 4×4 antenna elements with Chebyshev current distribution. The simulated and measured results show that the GAF antenna array has high gain of 18.2 dBi and −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1.52 GHz covering the range from 25.14 GHz to 26.66 GHz, which is much better than copper antenna array. In addition, the GAF antenna array has similar radiation patterns with copper antenna array, which indicates that the high conductivity GAF is a potential substitute for metal materials.

articleTitle: A Digital Retro-reflective Beamforming System Based on FPGA for Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: An experimental system of digital retro-reflective beamforming based on FPGA for wireless power transmission is presented. The wireless power transmission experiments involve the following three steps. First, pilot signal is broadcasted by a wireless power receiver as “request for wireless power.” Second, the pilot signals received by a wireless power transmitter are reversed in time. Third, the phase-conjugate signals are employed to construct a microwave power beam toward the location from which the pilot signal originates. To accomplish phase-conjugation, the pilot signals are down-converted to the baseband, then digitized and time-reversed by FPGA, and finally the time-reversed baseband signals are up-converted to the microwave frequency band. A least-absolute-value algorithm is implemented for time-reversal, which reduces the resource consumption of the FPGA. Experimental results demonstrate that the digital retro-reflective beamforming system is capable of constructing a wireless power beam toward the location of a mobile wireless power receiver in reaction to the pilot signal precisely.

articleTitle: Domain Knowledge Assisted Training Dataset Generation for Metasurface Designs
abstract: Domain knowledge assisted training dataset generation for deep learning aided metasurface designs is investigated. By combining the domain knowledge of metasurface from the designer and the advanced machine learning (ML) technique, an efficient training dataset generation approach has been successfully achieved. Unlike most existing metasurface generative designs that allow for arbitrary target pattern generation, which results in a time-consuming or even nonconvergence model training process, the proposed method takes the full advantages of the prior knowledge from designer to reduce the target solution space greatly, leading to reduced design cycles and higher explainabilities of the designs. The proposed ML model combines generative adversarial network (GAN) and variational autoencoder (VAE) as an encoder to transfer the original data into the latent space, which greatly improves the design efficiency as demonstrated in the validation results.

articleTitle: A Stopband-Improved Dual-Band Bandpass Defect Cavity Filter Using A Multimode ISGW Cavity
abstract: In this paper, a stopband-improved dual-band bandpass defect cavity filter based on Integrated Substrate Gap Wave-guide (ISGW) technology that has high integration but low insertion loss and self-encapsulation characteristic for suppressing EM interference is proposed. The single Rectangular ISGW Defect cavity that is perturbed by designing a metalized-cone has been designed by drugging rectangular cavity resonator in ISGW. Finally, the simulated result shows that: a 3-dB passband range of 1 st:27.68-~28.13GHz, f01=28.0 GHz, FBW=1.61 %; 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>: 31.875~33.195GHz, f02=32.0GHz, FBW=4.13%, the out-of-band suppression less than -20dB (18.5-27GHz). Two transmission zeros on both sides of the passband improve the frequency selectivity. The Group Delay(2,1) also shows flat in each passband compared with using SIW tech.

articleTitle: Swastika Hole shaped Phononic Crystal for Quality enhancement of Contour Mode Resonators
abstract: This study introduces a novel swastika hole shaped phononic crystal (SH-PnC) with wide acoustic band gap which can effectively hinder the propagation of acoustic energy through it. A delay line is used to check the transmission property of the proposed SH-PnC which shows a magnificent capability with more than 250 dB drop compared to a Si-bar based delay line. The FEM simulation results revealed that its employment on anchoring boundaries improved the Q-anchor (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">anc</sub>) and Q-unloaded (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) from 9295 and 7660 to 15450 and 11223 respectively. Furthermore, the insertion loss (IL) and motional resistance (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>) are improved from -11.4 dB and 123 Ω to -6 dB and 40 Ω respectively.

articleTitle: Acoustic Reflectors for Anchor Loss Reduction of Thin Film Piezoelectric on Substrate Resonators
abstract: This paper describes a fish scale reflector (FSR) structure in the anchoring boundaries to improve the quality factor of thin-film piezoelectric-on-substrate (TPoS) resonators. A 2D fishscale reflector is designed and employed on the anchoring boundaries aiming to suppress the acoustic energy leakage through the tether to the supporting substrate. Finite element method (FEM) simulated results revealed that compared to the conventional resonators, the resonators with single reflector and fish scale reflector has improved the quality factor. In this regard, the Q of the fish scale reflector (FSR) resonator achieved a 3.2-fold improvement (i.e. Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">anc</sub>=16366) compared with the conventional(C) design (i.e. Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">anc</sub>=5083) and an almost 2.3-fold improvement compared with the single reflector (SR) structure (i.e. Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">anc</sub> = 7044).

articleTitle: A 60 GHz Down-conversion Passive Mixer in 65 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: A passive down-conversion mixer in a 65nm buck CMOS process has been presented. The proposed mixer is consisted of a mixer-core and a folded OTA buffer. The mixer has a 3-dB bandwidth of 57~66 GHz, with a conversion gain of −2.7 ~ −5.4 dB. It requires a LO level of −5 dBm. The isolation between LO and RF ports is 10 dB. The total power consumption of the mixer is 1.4 mW, and the chip area is 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Based on 3-Coil Magnetic Resonance Coupling for Biomedical Implants
abstract: Electronic biomedical implants rely on wireless power transfer (WPT) systems to remove their dependency on chemical batteries to avoid potential safety issues. As traditional systems based on the inductive link are limited by their transmission distance, the magnetic resonance coupling (MRC) method for WPT has been proposed to increase the delivered power for mid-range applications. In this paper, we design a 3-coil magnetic resonant WPT system with a small power receiver for micro biomedical implants and evaluate its power transfer capability with a pork steak to mimic the attenuation caused by biological tissues. Operating at 180 kHz, the output of the proposed system can supply 56 mW at 3.3 V for an implanted receiver at a distance of 80 mm, which is 1.5 times more efficient than the traditional 2-coil system under the same conditions. Such a result demonstrates the applicability and improvement of the MRC-WPT system for powering up in-body biomedical devices.

articleTitle: A CMOS Low-Power Variable-Gain LNA Based on Triple Cascoded Common-Source Amplifiers and Forward-Body-Bias Technology
abstract: This paper presents a 15.8-30 GHz CMOS variable-gain LNA based on triple cascoded common-source (CS) amplifiers and forward-body-bias technology. The forward body bias (FBB) is utilized to effectively reduce the threshold voltage of the MOS transistor, and the minimum supply voltage for a MOSFET operating in the saturation region can be relaxed accordingly. Based on above strategy, a triple cascaded CS topology with low power is proposed with a 1.2 V standard power supply in 65-nm CMOS. In addition, the gain of the proposed topology can be adjusted via the body biasing, resulting in a variable-gain LNA successfully. For demonstration, a prototype of 15.8-30GHz variable-gain LNA is designed and fabricated in 65-nm CMOS technology with 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip size. The prototype achieves a minimum noise figure of 4.7 dB, a maximum gain of 11.4 dB with 16.4 dB gain tuning range, while consuming only 2.16 mW from a 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Spurious-Free Signal-Interference Dual-Band Bandpass Filters
abstract: The development of transversal signal-interference planar dual-band bandpass filters (BPFs) with extended upper stopband is addressed in this study. They are based on the exploitation of stepped-impedance-line transmission-line paths in their constituent dual-passband transversal filtering sections (TFSs) to “break” the spectral periodicity inherent to this type of filters in their traditional structures. A theoretical example of two-stage dual-band BPF derived through an optimization-based design procedure is provided to validate the approach, showing an upper-stopband bandwidth 18.1 times larger than in its classic counterpart. Moreover, a proof-of-concept prototype of this dual-band BPF design example is manufactured in microstrip technology and measured for experimental-demonstration purposes.

articleTitle: A Wide Tuning Range low Kvco Ka-Band BiCMOS LC-VCO Using Varactor Bank
abstract: A wide tuning rang, low K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VCO</inf> LC voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) is presented in this work. A pair of HBT is used to form a cross-coupled pair, working in the Class-C mode. In order to achieve low phase noise and wide tuning range at the same time, a 3-bits varactor bank and a varactor array are used to reduce the Kvco and make the tuning range as wide as possible. The proposed VCO is fabricated in 0.13 µm SiGe BiCMOS process with core area of 0.48×0.33 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The tuning range of the VCO is measured from 28.5 ~ 35 GHz (20.5%), and the phase noise at 1 MHz offset is better than −95 dBc/Hz. The peak output power is 6.2 dBm with the DC supply voltage of 1.8 V and current of 12.2mA.

articleTitle: Review of the Neural Network based Digital Predistortion Linearization of Multi-Band/MIMO Transmitters
abstract: This paper reviews the neural network (NN) based digital pre-distortion techniques for linearizing multi-band and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmitters. The most popular NN-based behavioral models using Deep Neural Networks (DNN), Augmented Neural Networks (ANN), and Shallow Neural Networks (SNN) will be reviewed. The paper will discuss NN-based DPD models using Real-Valued Focused Time-Delay Neural Network (RVFTDNN) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) performance and complexity for multi-band and MIMO applications. These models' performance will be assessed in terms of their capability to mitigate the transmitter's distortion and hardware impairments such as crosstalk, PA's nonlinearity, dc offset, and I/Q imbalance for multi-band and MIMO applications.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transmission (SWIPT) By Exploiting 2nd/3rd Harmonics
abstract: Far-field wireless power transmission always suffers from antenna radiation/polarization misalignment, and unknown distances between a base station and rectenna ends. To solve such problem, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>/3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics generated from RF-to-de rectification are exploited. Consequently, an interesting relationship between harmonic and radiation/polarization, distance can be established. To further realize high isolation between incidence and harmonic backscattered signals, novel diplexers are adopted. Together with a shared-aperture dual band antenna, a compact rectenna can be facilitated for high-efficiency simultaneous wireless information and power transmission (SWIPT) by exploiting 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>/3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy WiFi-Based 3D Indoor Positioning Using Non-Uniform Planar Array
abstract: With the development of mobile communication technology, location information has become more and more important for various services. Using a non-uniform planar array (NUPA), a WiFi-based three-dimensional indoor positioning system is proposed. The multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm is utilized to estimate the angle of arrival (AoA) of the direct ray, and then the time of flight is estimated with calibration data. An optimized NUPA is used for the antenna array in the access point. Experimental results show that the proposed positioning system achieves a median positioning error of 0.45 m in a complex indoor environment.

articleTitle: Digital Predistortion for Dual Linearly-Polarized Millimeter Wave Transmitters with Cross-Polarization Interference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel digital predistortion (DPD) technique that can simultaneously eliminate the cross-polarization interference (XPI) of dual linearly-polarized (DLP) antenna and inherent nonlinearities of power amplifiers (PAs) in millimeter wave transmitters. It is achieved by cascading the XPI cancellation module and nonlinear compensation module. The coefficients of both modules can be extracted from the decomposed over-the-air (OTA) signals. To validate the proposed idea, the experiment was carried out on a dual linearly-polarized (DLP) millimeter wave transmitter, and the results have shown that the XPI and nonlinearities can be effectively mitigated.

articleTitle: Dual-band Dual-polarized Scalable Phased Array Antenna with High Isolation and Polarization Purity for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized stacked patch antenna in package (AiP) operating at 28 and 39 GHz is proposed for 5G millimeter wave scalable phased array applications. With the isolation structure and differential feeding, the isolation between two polarization ports of the antenna element is greater than 50 dB, which is 10 dB higher than that without the isolation structure. Moreover, the cross-polarization isolation is greater than 30 dB. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the lower band starts from 27 to 28.4 GHz and the higher band covers the 38 to 39.5 GHz. The antenna has the advantages of simple structure, compact size and stable gain, making it suitable for the phased array antenna. Based on proposed antenna element, a 16-element phased array antenna, consisting of four scalable 2×2 subarrays, is designed. With simulations, it is proved that the antenna shows good beamforming performance in both frequency bands.

articleTitle: Theory and Practice of Multidimensional Non-Linear Transmission Line
abstract: Multidimensional non-linear transmission lines (NLTLs) have been studied and explored due to their outstanding capability of pulse generation and compression. In this connection, various types of NLTLs are theoretically investigated and developed including non-linear electrical transmission lines (NLETLs), gyromagnetic NLTLs, dielectric NLTLs, and magnetic NLTL. This study is set to provide comprehensive theoretical foundations, design perspectives, and recent developments of NLTLs for shorter and faster pulse generation and compression. Among them, NLETLs are described in detail with advanced models with comparison to the current state-of-the-art versions. Finally, the past studies of popular NLTL topologies are summarized and also the ongoing technological trends and future development opportunities in the field are briefly described.

articleTitle: Broadband Digital Predistortion Utilizing Parallel Quasi- Wiener-Hammerstein Model with Extended Dynamic Range
abstract: This paper proposes a low complexity and accurate behavioral modeling and digital predistortion (DPD) technique for broadband power amplifiers (PAs) utilizing a novel parallel quasi-Wiener-Hammerstein (PQWH) model. The PQWH model is formed by several quasi- Wiener-Hammerstein branches connected in parallel, thus it can efficiently extend the describable dynamic range and characterize of the nonlinear memory effect effectively. Compared to the generalized memory polynomial (GMP) where high-order memory depth is needed to describe the strong memory effect, the PQWH model consumes much lower computation complexity when linearizing a broadband PA. Experimental results on a 3.2-3.8 GHz GaN Doherty PA with a 100MHz OFDM signal show that the PQWH model can achieve a satisfied linearization performance while reducing over 70% coefficients compared to the GMP model.

articleTitle: A Fast Sparse Bayesian Pursuit Approach for Power Amplifier Linearization
abstract: In this paper, a fast pursuit algorithm based on a Bayesian approach is proposed for pruning behavioral models of power amplifiers (PAs). This approach, referred to as sparse Bayesian pursuit (SBP), is compared to two previously reported pruning algorithms: orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) and doubly OMP (DOMP). The three approaches are benchmarked with experimental data provided by a class AB PA driven by a 30-MHz 5G New Radio signal. The new sparse Bayesian pursuit approach outperforms the OMP in both modeling and linearization capabilities, while it reduces the computational cost with respect to the DOMP algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Vortex Reflectarray Based on Pancharatnam-Berry Metasurface
abstract: In this paper, a design of a wideband vortex reflec-tarray based on Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) metasurface is proposed, which consists of 20×20 elements. The patch is composed of an I-ring inlaid with an opening ring and is printed on the surface of the substrate. The other side of the substrate consist of a foam layer and a metal ground. A 360° reflection phase is achieved under the circularly polarized (CP) incidence. The simulation results show that the vortex beam carrying l=+2 orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode is successfully generated from 20-40 GHz, with an OAM bandwidth of 66.6%.

articleTitle: Multi-Section Support Vector Regression-Based Behavioral Modeling of RF GaN Doherty Power Amplifiers
abstract: A novel behavioral model based on multi-section support vector regression (MS-SVR) of radio frequency (RF) Gallium Nitride (GaN) Doherty power amplifiers (PAs) is proposed in this paper. In this method, the input signal is divided into different sections according to signal amplitude and each section is modeled separately using SVR. Experimental validation is performed using a 2.4 GHz Doherty PA. The results show that the proposed model can effectively reduce the time of parameter extraction and signal processing.

articleTitle: Efficient Detection of Rare Beacon Events in GEO Satellite Communication Systems using Deep Learning
abstract: Geosynchronous satellite (GEO) communications are highly susceptible to interference from environments such as rain, clouds, and hail. This exhibits a technical challenge to accurately detect the status of the weak Q-band (39.4 GHz) satellite beacon signals, which is critical for ensuring reliable satellite pointing using the ground station antenna. This paper exploits recent advances in deep learning to cope with this challenge. The proposed approach based on deep neural networks (DNN) and filtering (Filter-DNN) classifies rare events such as cloud, mist, rain as Non-line of sight (NLOS) and ordinary clear skies as Line of sight (LOS). Beacon data from a GEO satellite (Alphasat) ground station under two different attenuation conditions is used for validation. The experimental results show that our method can detect the rare event with an accuracy score of 92% by using only 2000 data sample points, while conventional approaches such as MUSIC require about 100k sample points to maintain detection. These results indicate that the proposed technique could be a promising tool for achieving satisfactory results in space exploration and gain insights into GEO satellite communication problems.

articleTitle: Switchable Dual-Band Bandpass Filter with High Selectivity
abstract: In this paper, a novel switchable dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) with high selectivity is proposed. Half wavelength resonators and open stub loaded resonators are employed to provide third-order filtering responses in each band. By utilizing stepped-impedance open stubs and one-end-shorted couple lines, the individual passband signal can be suppressed independently with switches. In addition, the proposed coupling topology introduces multiple transmission zeros providing high frequency selectivity and good out-of-band rejection. The proposed switchable filter is implemented with two passbands centered at 2.90GHz and 4.79GHz with a low insertion loss of 1.2 dB and 1.1 dB, respectively, providing band-edge steepness over 97.7 dB/GHz. Four operating modes (dual-band, no band, high band, and low band) are achieved by controlling the states of passbands with switches.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Electrically Small Antenna With Reconfigurable Radiation Pattern
abstract: A single-layer, ultra-low-profile, electrically small, pattern-reconfigurable antenna is presented. The antenna consists of electric and magnetic dipole elements and a reconfigurable driven element. Six p-i-n diodes are integrated into the driven element to obtain three switchable endfire radiation states, each state covers more than 120°, which covers the entire 360° azimuth plane. For verification, a pattern reconfigurable antenna was fabricated and tested. The antenna exhibits the following measured results: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{a}= 0.75$</tex> electrical size, 2.9% fractional impedance bandwidth, 4.17dBi peak gain, front-to-back ratios (FTRB) ~21.2dB, and radiation efficiencies (RE) ~82.6% for three switchable endfire radiation states.

articleTitle: Aperture Phase GA Optimization for Reflectarray Antennas with Feed Lateral Displacement
abstract: In this paper, an aperture phase optimization method using genetic algorithm (GA) for a reflectarray (RA) with a horizontal moving feed is presented. To improve the beam-scanning performance of the RA, the gain and BWFN (beam width between first nulls) of uv planar are introduced as key indicators in the phase optimization to reduce the gain variation. A full-wave simulation has been carried out to verify the method, and the results show that the gain variation of the optimized RA is smaller than 2 dB within ±30° scan coverage, while it is 4.6 dB for the traditional narabolic design.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Shielded Dual-band SIW Filter Based on Novel Slotlines with High Selectivity and Controllable Transmission Zeros
abstract: This study proposes a miniaturized dual-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter by loading novel slot line resonators. These slotlines divide the whole SIW cavity into two identical resonators. The fundamental mode is used to form the first passband and the higher mode forms the second passband. The center frequencies of both passbands are below the cut-off frequency of the original SIW cavity. Miniaturization is thus achieved. Two transmission zeros are introduced by source-to-load coupling, therefore achieving the harmonic suppressing and good out-of-band rejection. A prototype is fabricated and measured, and the measured result agrees well with the simulated data. This filter exhibits good performance including compact size, low loss and good out-of-band suppression.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Efficiency Ku/Ka Dual-Band Power Amplifier
abstract: A novel design of a Ku/Ka dual-band power amplifier is presented. A duplexer structure based on high-pass and low-pass filters is selected as the input stage for frequency selection of the input signal. The output stage of the power amplifier adopts a dual-frequency matching network, and the independent matching of the two frequency bands is realized through a section of impedance transformation line. Measurement results show that the amplifier can achieve an output power of over 41dBm and a PAE of over 32% in the 12-18GHz range when operating in Ku-band mode, and over 33dBm and a PAE of over 27% in the 31-36GHz range when operating in Ka-band mode.

articleTitle: Analysis of Asymmetric Modulating Pulse on SSB-TMA
abstract: In most researches about time-modulated array (TMA), modulating pulses are usually considered as the rectangular, symmetric trapezoidal or triangular waveform. Due to the nonideal characteristics of RF switches and circuits, the shape of modulated pulse is usually asymmetric. This paper analyzes the influence of the asymmetry of trapezoid and TDRC waveforms on SSB-TMA in detail, and compares the amplitude, phase, energy ratio and relative SBL of the harmonics. The results show that the asymmetry of the trapezoid and TDRC waveforms will affect the amplitude and phase of the +1st harmonics, and also will worsen the −3rd harmonics.

articleTitle: A Software-Adaptive 77GHz Radar Sensor for Traffic Applications
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar sensors applied in traffic scenarios are mainly divided into two categories: real-time speed control and traffic monitoring as an all-weather sensor of intelligent transportation infrastructure components. This work presents the design, implementation, and verification procedure of a software-adaptive 77 GHz radar sensor, which can meet both mentioned traffic applications. The implemented radar sensor can adapt itself to one “longer distance (300 m) narrow FoV (± 3°) “mode or to the other” shorter distance (200 m) wide FoV (± 10°) “mode by switching operational modes via software but based on exactly the same hardware platform. The radar coverage diagrams were measured for both operational modes. Measurement results in real traffic scenarios confirmed functions of the implemented traffic radar from system performance aspect. Additionally, a real-time calibration procedure based on stationary object detection was also proposed and verified as practical solution for convenient installation. A co-integration product form with camera was implemented for further data fusion.

articleTitle: A Ku-band Tunable Absorptive Frequency Selective Reflector
abstract: In this paper, a Ku-band tunable absorptive frequency selective reflector (TAFSR) is proposed. The TAFSR has a sandwich structure: an active resistive sheet at the top layer, and PEC at the bottom layer, divided by F4B substrate. The resistive sheet layer is composed of a simple straight strip between two metallic strips with PIN diodes loaded to get the tunable reflective coefficient. PIN diodes can be equivalent to serial RL circuit. Two metallic strips and the gap between units is equivalent to serial LC circuit to control the resonant center frequency. The biased strip can be equivalent to the parallel inductance circuit as the electric structure and the biased lines simultaneously. The influence of the PIN diodes' tunable resistance is analyzed through equivalent circuit model. The measurement results show that the -10dB tunable absorptive band of the proposed TAFSR can be achieved in Ku-band from 10.3 GHz to 19.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Neural Network Technique for Microwave Parametric Modeling
abstract: Nowadays, the advent of deep learning techniques has enabled neural networks to adapt to more challenging models. However, it takes excessively long time to develope deep neural networks (DNNs) used for microwave component parametric modeling, which reduces its practicality. This paper proposes a new technique to speed up the process of developing such DNNs. Batch normalization (BN) technique is proposed to improve the convergence of the sigmoid networks and effectively alleviate the gradient vanishing problem. We use the BN layers alternately with the sigmoid layers instead of the pure sigmoid network. Furthermore, we propose to adopt the leaky ReLU (L·ReLU) to solve the neuron death problem, which can reduce the computation and training time by 52.0% and 69.7% respectively. We show an example of wide-range microwave parametric modeling to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Low-frequency Tunable Multi-Band Mobile Phone Antenna for LTE and 5G Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel mobile phone antenna with a metal rim for LTE/WWAN/5G band is proposed, which is low-frequency, tunable and multi-band. The antenna is composed of a controlling circuit for the varactor and the monopole and loop branch strips. The overall antenna radiation performance could be optimized and enhanced through the metal rim and a lumped component matching circuit. It is fabricated on the FR-4 PCB substrate. It is showed that the antenna can get a -6dB bandwidth covering the LTE/5G bands from 700MHz to 6GHz. The radiation efficiency of low-frequency is more than 30% (-5dB). And it varies from 46% to 76% for the 1.7GHz to 6GHz high band. It features tunable low band without affecting the high frequency part.

articleTitle: Retro-reflective Beamforming based on a Frequency Division Scheme for Microwave Power Transmission to Multiple Targets
abstract: This paper presents an experimental retro-reflective beamforming system for wireless power transmission to multiple targets (with “targets” standing for “wireless power receivers” in this paper). In our experiments, each target broadcasts a pilot signal at a unique frequency. The pilot signals from multiple targets are received by a wireless power transmitter. After analyzing the pilot signals, the wireless power transmitter configures one power beam toward each target at its pilot signal's frequency based on phase-conjugation. With a digital beamforming circuit architecture, multiple retro-reflective beams at multiple frequencies can be formed simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed retro-reflective beamforming scheme based on frequency division could track multiple targets' location and construct multiple power beams accordingly.

articleTitle: High Selectivity Filtering Patch Antenna Using Parasitic Patches
abstract: A filtering patch antenna based on parasitic patches is proposed in this paper. The filtering antenna is mainly composed of a driven patch, a parasitic rectangular patch, and a parasitic ring patch. The combination of the driven patch and parasitic rectangular patch can create a radiation null at the upper band edge, while the addition of parasitic ring patch can introduce another radiation null at the lower band edge. The propose antenna exhibits a quasi-elliptic boresight gain response with the help the two radiation nulls. The simulated| S11| of the proposed antenna is less than −10 dB in the range of 0.92-1.08 GHz (16%). Without extra filtering circuits, the antenna achieves an average simulated gain of 9.3 dBi within passband.

articleTitle: K-band 360° Passive Vector Modulator Phase Shifter with Coupled Line Qadrature Coupler and Passive Transistor Array
abstract: This letter introduces a passive vector modulator phase shifter fabricated by 65-nm CMOS technology. Coupled line quadrature coupler is used to obtain broader bandwidth and more accurate quadrature signals. This work sums up an integrated method to analyze and improve the performance of the passive transistor array, and focuses on the impact of the matching impedance of the transistor array on the circuit performance. The proposed vector modulator phase shifter achieves a phase shift with range of 360° by 5.625° step, and an insertion loss of 11-14dB from 16-26GHz. The minimal RMS of phase error is 1.2° at 21GHz, and the maximum loss difference is 2dB in working frequency.

articleTitle: Long-range MIMO Communication Using Plane Spiral OAM Mode-group
abstract: A communication prototype of plane spiral OAM (PSOAM) mode-group (MG) based multiple-in-multiple-out (MIMO) system is built in a line-of-sight (LoS) scenario. Then, a long-range wireless transmission experiment is conducted at a distance of 30 m (beyond Rayleigh distance). The bit-error-rate (BER) performance proves the feasibility of the proposed system. The obtainable single-way spectrum efficiency is 3.7 bits/s/Hz/stream. MG's vorticity can provide another controllable degree of free (DoF) to reduce the spatial correlation, it's more suitable for the long-range wireless transmission relative to conventional OAM multiplexing technique.

articleTitle: A K-Band Variable Gain Low-Noise Amplifier with Low Phase Variation in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: Based on the inductive source degenerated cascode amplifier gain cell, a two-stage variable gain K-band low noise amplifier (LNA) with low phase variation is designed for wireless communication. With the transformer-based matching network and current steering variable gain techniques, theoretical analysis and simulations are undertaken, revealing and verifying the way to achieve wide bandwidth and low phase variation. Over 19-to-23 GHz, test results show that the proposed circuit achieves 4.5-to-18.5-dB power gain, 4.1-dB noise figure (NF) and 14.5 dBm OIP3. For a low phase variation, less than 1.8° RMS phase error can be achieved with 6dB gain variation from 19 to 23 GHz. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process, the LNA consumes 67.2 mW from a 1.2 V supply and its chip size (including all pads) is 0.8×0.48 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of 1-bit Programmable Holographic Metasurface for Monopulse Radar Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design of 1-bit programmable holographic metasurface (PHMS) concept for monopulse radar applications. A 1-bit programmable unit-cell with only one PIN diode, which can tune the surface impedance for high impedance or low impedance mode as the PIN diode flipped, is proposed. Holographic patterning technique is employed to realize the sum (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma$</tex>) and difference (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>) patterns based on the proposed PHMS. A 20×20 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\lambda_{0}\times 5\lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the wavelength at 10.0 GHz) PHMS is built and analyzed using a commercial full-wave simulator. The simulated results suggest that two-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma$</tex> pattern scanning and one-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> pattern scanning within ±40° are achieved, which can be applied for tracking radar enabled by monopulse technique.

articleTitle: A 77-GHz Fully Integrated Power Amplifier for Automotive Radar Application in 40-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a compact 77-GHz four-way differential power combined power amplifier for automotive radar application. At E-band, the insertion loss of matching network and power combining network are the limiting factor for the power amplifier's performance. In this work, the insertion loss of the matching networks is reduced by taking advantage of the proposed coplanar waveguide differential transmission line with floating substrate noise shielding grids. The voltage-current power combining method that takes care of impedance matching and power combining is adopted to decrease the insertion loss from power combining and output matching network. The power amplifier is implemented in a 40 nm CMOS process. From 69 to 85 GHz, the power amplifier delivers more than 19 dBm output power with the maximum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{sat}$</tex> of 19.7 GHz at 77 GHz. The final layout power amplifier achieves 19.4 dB peak small signal gain, and the maximum PAE is 22.7 %.

articleTitle: Deep Digital Signal Recovery for LEO Satellite Communication in Presence of System Perturbations
abstract: This paper proposes a deep neural network (DNN)-based digital signal recovery (DSR) technique for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications. Different from existing work, which only investigates impacts of the satellite-to-ground communication channel, this work focuses on handling the nonlinearity variations caused by input power level perturbations in the transmitter. The system is validated using a high gain radio frequency power amplifier (RF-PA) operating at 28.5 GHz, where perturbations are introduced by varying the power level of the input signal, from -39 dBm to -31 dBm, to the RF-PA. Experimental results show that the DNN trained at an input power level of -35 dBm achieved an improvement of 7.52 dB in the adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR), and an improvement of 4.2% in error vector magnitude (EVM). Applying the DDN trained at -35 dBm to other cases demonstrates that a 1 dB power level perturbation only leads to ≈ 1 dB degradation of the ACLR and ≈ 1.6% degradation of the EVM, respectively, which indicates the potential of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Portable 5.8 GHz Radar Sensor with an Integreted Common-Aperture Single Antenna for Noncontact Physiological Monitoring
abstract: In this paper, a portable 5.8 GHz Doppler radar with an integrated common aperture single antenna is proposed for noncontact monitoring of physiological signals such as respiration and heartbeat. The conventional Doppler radar system usually employs two separate transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) antennas for improved Tx/Rx isolation. However, it inevitably adds up to the size of the radar system. By leveraging the characteristics of the rat-race coupler, a common-aperture antenna was designed and integrated together with the radar transceiver on a single printed circuit board (PCB), which dramatically reduces the size of the entire radar system. The proposed antenna's Tx/Rx isolation at 5.8 GHz is measured to be higher than 35 dB. Compared with the conventional two separate antennas with similar isolation, the size of the proposed single antenna is reduced by 160% and the entire radar system is reduced in area by 80% with a size of only 10 cmˣ5 cm. Experiments were carried out in the office environment to wirelessly detect human vital signs. It was demonstrated that the proposed portable radar system integrated with a common-aperture single antenna can successfully capture the physiological signals of respiration and heartbeat.

articleTitle: Power amplifier design considerations using a simplified model for the transistor
abstract: This paper discusses the use of a simplified static model for representing high-frequency transistors in the initial stage of power amplifier design. Focusing on gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors, the application of the model to two different scenarios is shown. Firstly, the model is proven to be effective in initiating the design of a broadband PA for Ku-band, and results are compared to the use of a full non-linear model showing a good agreement. Secondly, the model is used to analyze the sensitivity to load mismatch of different PA architectures, including balanced, Doherty, and load-modulated balanced amplifiers and offering some interesting insight into this very relevant problem in modern wireless transmitters.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Standard Physical Models of GaN HEMTs: MVSG and ASM
abstract: In this paper, two standard physics-based compact models of GaN HEMTs, MVSG-RF and ASM-HEMT, are compared. The current voltage (I-V) output characteristics and capacitance voltage (C-V) characteristics of a depletion-mode GaN device with channel length of 0.25 μm, gate width of 125 μm and gate finger of 2 were simulated and compared with experimental data to verify the validity of the two models. From the results, it is observed that both MVSG and ASM accurately model the DC performances of the device, but the model precision of AC characteristics is still insufficient. Finally, Load-Pull simulation is carried out.

articleTitle: A 24 GHz MIMO PMCW Automotive Radar with Doppler Compensation
abstract: In this paper, a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) phase-modulated continuous wave (PMCW) radar system is modeled and analyzed. The operating frequency at 24 GHz band with 1 GHz bandwidth is selected for Medium Range Radar (MRR) scenarios. Basic PMCW principles are reviewed. Key parameters of the proposed RF system and signal processing chain are verified in MATLAB. For high-speed target detections, an extra doppler compensation procedure is required to boost the accuracy of angle processing. Final simulation results of the target distance, velocity and direction of angle are shown.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Shielding Analysis of Different Grounded Bump Distribution in SiP
abstract: In this paper, a strategy for improving the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of System-in-Package (SiP) by optimizing the distribution of grounded bumps is presented, where the full-wave simulation is applied to obtain electromagnetic radiation under different grounded bump distributions in SiP. The shielding performance of the package with different grounded bumps distributions is further analyzed. Then the gap between signal bumps and the ground plane is modeled as a rectangular waveguide. Moreover, the reason why the shielding performance of different model changes is explained. Finally, this paper draws a method to improve the overall shielding performance of the package. As a result, this work can guide the optimal design of Integrated Circuits (IC) package.

articleTitle: Fast Target Localization Method for FMCW MIMO Radar
abstract: The conventional two-dimensional multiple signal classification (2D-MUSIC) algorithm for frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar target localization is lack of real-time. In this paper, a forward-backward spatial smoothing (SS) based linear prediction-orthogonal propagator method (LP-OPM) is proposed for target localization. Direction-of-arrival (DOA) and range are estimated independently by SS-LP-OPM algorithm, and then the parameters are matched by least squares (LS). Among them, SS technique improves the Toeplitz and Hermitian characteristics of the covariance matrix of the received data, thereby improving the accuracy of using LP to reconstruct the diagonal elements of the covariance, and reducing the impact of noise. At the same time, because OPM neither needs to increase the data dimension or calculate eigenvalue decomposition, the real-time localization is guaranteed. The superiority of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulation and experiment results.

articleTitle: Design of 24-30 GHz GaN Power Amplifiers with Harmonic-controlled Matching Network
abstract: Two monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifiers (PAs) using 0.1 um GaN process are presented in this work. The PAs are designed to work from 24 to 30 GHz, covering the frequencies like 24.25-27.5 GHz, 27.5-28.35 GHz and 27.5-29.1 GHz for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) bands. A harmonic-controlled output matching method is used to improve bandwidth and efficiency for two PAs, one is a single stage PA and the other is a two-stage two-way combined PA. The single stage PA has a first measurement results of 25 dBm output power and 25% power-added efficiency (PAE), which are 3.5 dB and 11 % lower than the simulation results. The total sizes of the chips are 1.05*0.65 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 1.75*1.25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The single stage PA is packaged and the measured results agree with the simulated results in terms of small signal performance.

articleTitle: Air Bubble Detection Based on Portable mm- Wave Doppler Radars
abstract: This paper provides a feasibility study for the noncontact detection and monitoring for the presence of moving gas phases in gas-liquid flows based on portable mm-wave Doppler radars. The identification of moving gas phases is of paramount importance in a large range of areas such as petroleum, biomedical, and food processing industries. Several experiments were carried out to verify the feasibility of the non-invasive air bubbles detection using Doppler radars. The mm-wave radar sensor captures and down-converts the microwave signal, which is phase-modu-lated by the linear motion of the air-water interface inside the pipe. The high sensitivity of the mm-wave radar sensor also allows the estimation of the speed of the air bubbles.

articleTitle: Design of Doherty Power Amplifier Using Load-pull X-Parameters
abstract: The design of Doherty power amplifier (DPA) using load-pull X-parameter model is demonstrated in this paper. A 10 W GaN HEMT transistor is employed for the PA designing. As soon as the X-parameter model is extracted, its performance is validated. Compared with the circuit model provided by the device manufacture, the used X-parameters gives an excellent prediction. The region of the load Smith chart leads to optimal output power and drain efficiency (DE) can be accurately identified as critical to amplifier design. The input and output matching networks are designed using a Chebyshev low-pass architecture, and a step-im-pedance converter structure is used to design the output synthesis network. Finally, a DPA was designed and fabricated. The realized DPA achieves a saturation output power over 41 dBm in the frequency band of 1.4 GHz - 1.6 GHz, a saturation DE over 58%, and 6dB output power back-off (OBO) efficiency over 46%. The comparison between the measured results of the realized DPA and the used load-pull X-parameter model is also given, and it shows that the X-parameter model can be applied for DPA designing with high-fidelity.

articleTitle: Novel High Gain W-band Antenna Array Using Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
abstract: In this paper, a W-band high gain 4×4 slot-enhanced antenna array is proposed based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW). The antenna array is composed of four 2×2 slot-enhanced antenna subarrays, and each subarray is excited by a high-order mode TE220 within a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity using PCB technology. The feeding network based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW) can reduce the transition loss. The gain of the designed antenna is more than 18 dBi and the peak gain reaches 19.7 dBi for the impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: High-efficiency Millimeter-wave Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Using Metasurface
abstract: In this manuscript, a new type of high-efficiency compact metasurface linear antenna array using low-loss seri-al-parallel feed is proposed. It operates at 24GHz ± 0.5GHz and the in-band efficiency is greater than 82%. Based on it, the linear array is compactly arranged with a small distance of 0.4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to realize wide-angle phased array. In order to avoid the influence of coupling between adjacent linear arrays on the scanning performance, the width of the metasurface is very narrow and several metal walls are loaded, thus isolation between adjacent linear arrays is higher than 20dB. The results show that the proposed phased array can achieve a scanning range of -60~60°, and the in-band efficiency is larger than 77%, which would be potentially applied in future wireless energy transmission systems.

articleTitle: A New Calculation Method of Correction Factor for Microcalorimeters
abstract: In calibration measurement of RF power sensor, effective efficiency directly measured requires further correction to compensate external power loss. Correction factor is hence introduced, to convert uncorrected effective efficiency to real effective efficiency of power sensor. In conventional calculation method, insertion loss of transmission line connected to sensor is neglected, due to its relatively small value. Yet for higher frequency band, insertion loss undergoes rapid increase. Hence conventional calculation method of correction factor results in an unacceptable calculation error. This paper presents a new calculation method of correction factor, valid for high frequency power measurement. Correction factor increases up to 5% with proposed method applied. Subsequently, an iterative algorithm for correction factor is introduced, achieving precise correction factor results via computer software.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach Applied in the Optimization of the Switched Filter Bank's Gain Flatness
abstract: A novel approach applied in the optimization of the switched filter bank's gain flatness is introduced. The original, first and second optimizational design of switched filter bank is firstly presented, then, field-circuit co-simulation based on Computer Simulation Technology (CST) and Advanced Design System (ADS) is demonstrated. Finally, the measurement data are given, which are in excellent agreement with the simulation. The measured gain flatness of the first optimizational case is 0.11dB better than the original one. Simultaneously, the measured gain flatness of the second optimizational case is 1.13dB better than the original one. As a conclusion, a novel approach optimizing the switched filter bank's gain flatness with practical engineering values is presented, demonstrating the precise analysis of a switched filter bank.

articleTitle: Q/V Dual-Band Filter with Perturbation in Single Substrate Integrated Waveguide Circular Cavity
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter with perturbed circular cavity is presented. By introducing a pair of metallic via perturbations combining different angle of feeding lines, five resonant modes TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> (a pair of degenerate modes), TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</inf> (a pair of degenerate modes) and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">020</inf> are perturbed to design the proposed filter. Two types of slotlines are introduced to cavity for tuning the resonant modes. Thus, a dual-band filter with two transmission poles in the first passband and three transmission poles in the second passband is realized in a single circular cavity. The experimental result shows that the center frequencies of the dual-band filter are 42.7 and 60 GHz, and the 3-dB FBWs are 6.6% and 7.8%, respectively. The measured minimum in-band insertion losses are around 1 and 1.88 dB, and the passband return losses are above 19.6 and 11 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Tri-band Dual-circularly Polarized BeiDou Navigation Antenna Based on Metamaterial
abstract: A tri-band dual-circularly polarized BeiDou navigation antenna based on metamaterial structure is proposed and designed in this paper. The antenna is a square loop which consists of four double periodic bridged composite right / left handed (DP B-CRLH) metamaterial unit cells, and is fed by single feed point. The DP B-CRLH unit cell which has multi-band and right / left handed propagation characteristics was used to realize the tri-band dual-circularly polarized antenna. The measured results show that the antenna receives right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) navigation signals in B2 band; radiates left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) short message communication signals in L band; receives RHCP short message communication signals in S band, simultaneously, and the bandwidths of axial ratio less than 3 dB are about 10%, 7.4% and 2.8%, respectively. S11<; -10dB in the three operating frequency bands, meeting the official performance standard requirements of BeiDou navigation antenna.

Author Keywords: Composite right / left handed transmission line

articleTitle: Parameter Extraction and Modeling of Schottky Diodes: An Extension of the Resonance Based Inductance Extraction Method
abstract: In this paper, a full parameter extraction flow of Schottky diodes is proposed as the extension of previous resonance-based inductance extraction method. This extraction flow is applied to the model development of MACOM MA4E1317 and shows satisfying modeling accuracy. The full parameters of MA-COM MA4E1317 are extracted and provided, which also helps solve current dilemma of lacking accurate high-frequency Schottky diode models.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Parallel QC-LDPC Encoder
abstract: In this paper, a low complexity parallel QC (quasi-cyclic)-LDPC (low-density parity-check) Codes encoding algorithm and encoder architecture is introduced. In traditional encoder architectures, the complexity of multiplication operation of information sequence and generator matrix is very high. The proposed encoding algorithm bit selection (BS) directly selects the valid information bits according to position set of non-zero elements in the first column of the sub-matrix, which avoids the operation of invalid information bits. The proposed parallel QC-LDPC encoder architectures is realized for FPGA implementation based on CCSDS (7154, 8176) LDPC codes.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Waveguide Slot Antenna with Dual-band Rejection
abstract: A dual-band rejection rectangular waveguide transmission line is introduced, where two stopbands are achieved by T-type and II-type resonators loading at the bottom wall of the rectangular waveguide. The frequencies and bandwidths of the two stopbands can be tuned by adjusting parameters of resonators. To verify this concept, a rectangular waveguide filtering four-slot antenna with two stopbands is designed and simulated. Compared with a traditional rectangular waveguide four-slot antenna, the simulated results show that the proposed filtering antenna operates well in 5.6-5.9 GHz and realizes suppression levels stronger than 39.9 dB and 51.9 dB in 6.6-7.1 GHz and 8.4-9.3 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band −200.2-dBc/Hz FoMT Low-Power Low-Phase-Noise LC-VCO IC with a Novel Feedback Circuit Using the Leakage Current
abstract: A Ku-band low-power low-phase-noise LC-VCO IC with a novel feedback circuit is presented in this paper. The novel feedback circuit controls a bias voltage to the VCO core circuit to reduce the dc power consumption and guarantees the robust start-up of the oscillation. The leakage current is utilized to drive the feedback circuit so that the dc power consumption in the feedback circuit is suppressed. The proposed Ku-band LC-VCO IC has exhibited a measured phase noise of −133.9 dBc/Hz, an FoM of −192.0 dBc/Hz, and an FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of −200.2 dBc/Hz under the maximum total Power consumption of 2.98 mW.

articleTitle: Half Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide and Microstrip Rectangular Patch Hybrid Integrated Coupler
abstract: In this paper, a half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) and microstrip rectangular patch (MRP) hybrid integrated coupler with two HMSIW ports and two microstrip ports is presented. The HMSIW ports are compatible with HMSIW components (e.g. HMSIW antennas), while the microstrip ports are compatible with active devices (e.g. power amplifiers). Due to the compact geometry and great compatibility with various topologies, the proposed hybrid integrated coupler is attractive for the design of active antennas, balanced amplifiers, six-port receivers, etc. To verify the proposed scheme, a 3-dB prototype coupler is designed, fabricated and measured, which achieves a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 21 % with 1 dB amplitude imbalance and 4° phase imbalance.

articleTitle: Quad-Band Impedance Transformer for Extremely High Load Impedance Matching with Out-of-Band Spurious Response Suppression
abstract: A novel approach to design a quad-band impedance transformer (QBIT) is presented. The primary purpose of this transformer is to match an extremely high load impedance to a source impedance of 50Ω at four distinct frequency bands with suppression of the spurious passband. The proposed QBIT is constructed using a π-shaped topology and two series microstrip-lines. The ABCD matrix method is employed to derive closed-form design formulas. The latter are employed to obtain the circuit parameters that allow for matching extremely high load impedances. For validation, two prototypes of QBIT realized to match 500Ω and 1500Ω loads are fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured transformer characteristics are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A Compact Polarization and Pattern Reconfigurable Patch Antenna by Digital Coding Method
abstract: A compact array antenna employing polarization and radiation pattern reconfigurable with digital coding method is presented. The antenna unit consists of a square patch loaded by four 1-pf capacitors and four switchable feeding ports which are controlled by a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). By designing the coding modes of the digital radiating units, four different radiation beams with three linear polarization states of (+45°-LP, −45°-LP, and V-LP) can be realized by switching the corresponding coding sequences.

articleTitle: A Two-dimensional Multibeam Antenna Array Based on SIW Butler Matrices
abstract: In this paper, a wideband two-dimensional (2-D) 16×16 Butler matrix based multibeam antenna array in the range from 24GHz to 28GHz is presented for 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) applications. The 16 beams are controlled by two stages of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) Butler matrices placed orthogonally. Each output port of the first-stage Butler matrices stacked vertically is twisted 90 degrees and connected to the corresponding input port of the second-stage Butler matrices stacked horizontally. The novel 2-D interconnection method is implemented based on the flexibility of the SIW without any connectors, cables and soldering operations, and then possesses the advantages of low cost, extensible and integrated easily in the mmWave bands.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-Based Wideband Dual-Circular-Polarized Dual-Port Antenna for SWIPT Application
abstract: This paper presents a wideband dual-port dual-circular-polarized antenna that operates at 2.45 GHz and 6 GHz for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer systems. The higher frequency band at 5 GHz – 7 GHz is designed for RF energy transmission, while the lower frequency band at 2.45 GHz is designed for wireless communication. The patch that operates at higher band is covered by a metasurface, in order to extend the bandwidth. The radiators that operate at higher and lower bands share the same aperture, and the radiator operating at lower frequency (the square patch) also acts as the ground of the radiator that operates at higher band (4-element patch array). The proposed antenna is implemented. In the measurement, 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth is found of 43% (from 4.7 to 7.3 GHz), and an isolation better than 45 dB is found at 2.45 GHz. The average gain exceeds 9.5 dBi from 5 GHz at 7GHz and 9 dBi at 2.45 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: Sample Selection Method for Digital Predistortion with Incremental Dimension of Coefficients
abstract: In this paper, we present a new method for the linearization of radio frequency (RF) power amplifies (PAs) based on the sample selection method (SSM) with incremental dimension of coefficients. In SSM, insufficient training samples can cause some problems such as the low convergence speed and serious noise interference. In order to solve these problems, we propose to use coefficient vectors with increasing dimension in iterations and then to introduce the dimension reduction (or pruning) technique to ensure the priority selections of important coefficients in training. Experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve better normalized mean square error (NMSE) and adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) with faster convergence speed compared with SSM.

articleTitle: A Highly-integrated Non-magnetic Passive Circulator Based on Rotary Traveling-wave Oscillator and Spatio-temporal Conductivity Modulation in 130 nm CMOS
abstract: A fully-integrated non-magnetic passive circulator for full-duplex wireless communication application is presented in this letter. The proposed design is based on spatio-temporal conductivity modulation to achieve non-reciprocity. This circulator also utilizes on-chip quadrature clock signals generated by a rotary traveling-wave oscillator, so it is featured with low-cost and highly integrated. Implemented 130 nm CMOS standard process, the 9 GHz Circulator achieves antenna (ANT) -to-receiver (RX) and transmitter (TX)-to-ANT insertion losses of −3.9 dB and −2.5 dB, respectively, with TX-to-RX isolation of 13.4-18.1 dB. This chip occupies a core area of 1.68 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while the core power consumption is 38.6 mW with a supply of 1.2 V.

articleTitle: Linearization of GaN HEMT-Based Power Amplifiers Using a Bias Tracking Digital Predistortion
abstract: In this paper, a novel bias tracking (BT) digital predistortion (DPD) scheme for the compensation of charge-trapping effects in GaN HEMT -based power amplifiers (PAs). In the BT DPD scheme, a piece-wise polynomial (PMP) model is proposed in the digital domain to model the compensation bias voltage that is injected into the P A's gate bias and mask the gain changes caused by long-term charge-trapping effects.
