The proposed BT compensation method was demonstrated with a series of pulse-modulated LTE signals on a class-AB GaN HEMT-based P A. Measurement results indicated the proposed BT DPD scheme outperformed the conventional DPD method in linearization performances.

articleTitle: A Compact Mixed-Mode 62 GHz Doherty Power Amplifier with 28.9% Peak PAE and 14.2 dBm OP1dB Using Dynamic Power Allocation
abstract: This paper presents a 62 GHz, mixed-mode compact Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) with high linearity and efficiency implemented in a 65-nm CMOS technology. The DPA adopts a novel linearity boosting and efficiency enhancement technique by introducing a dynamic-power-allocation mechanism which is realized by a coupler-based power divider and a mixed-mode DPA architecture. By adjusting the control voltages of the PA in the gain stage, the input power allocated to both paths change, leading to a measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$OP_{1dB}$</tex> increase from 11.72 dBm to 14.2 dBm, a maximum 15.6 dBm output power and a 9.09% PAE improvement at the 1-dB compression point. A novel compact three-coil-coupled transformer along with an output matching capacitor are proposed as the power combiner, output matching network, balun, and impedance inverter. The core part of the fabricated DPA occupies an area of 0.04 mm2, exhibits a 15.6 dBm saturated output power, a peak power gain of 19 dB, an OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of 14.2 dBm, with a 28.9% peak power-added efficiency (PAE), and a 27.2% PAE at 1-dB compression point, and a 12.7% PAE at 6-dB back-off. The DC power consumption of the PA is only 68 mW.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Rat-Race Hybrid Using Combined Slot-Coupled Balun and Power Divider
abstract: A wideband rat-race hybrid is proposed in this paper. Out-of-phase Marchand balun and in-phase power divider is combined to realize hybrid response with bandwidth enhanced using slot-coupled resonators. A prototype hybrid centered at 3 GHz is fabricated to validate the design. Measured and simulated results are in good agreement, demonstrating that the proposed rat-race hybrid has fractional bandwidth of 64% and 45.2% at Σ- and Δ-port with low insertion loss and imbalance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Nonlinear Digital Interference Cancellation with Two-Dimensional Orthogonalization for Co-site radios
abstract: The performance of traditional adaptive nonliear interference cancellation algorithms will degrade in practical application due to the correlation of nonliear basis function. Therefore, in this paper, we proposed a two dimensional orthogonalization based adaptive nonlinear digital interference cancellation algorithm. In the proposed algorithm, the input signals is first orthogonalized, then a new nonliear basis function is formalized and orthogonalized to minimizing the correlation. With the two-dimensional orthogonalized basis function, a least mean square (LMS) based parameter learning approach is developed to efficiently estimate the coefficients of the nonlinear cancellation filter. Simulation results show that, comparing with traditional orthogonalization based algorithm, the proposed method can suppress interference signal more efficiently and achieve stable state more quickly in present of high nonlinearity.

articleTitle: AMetallic Shield-free Tri-mode Dielectric Resonator Filter
abstract: In this paper, a tri-mode dielectric resonator filter is implemented with metallic shield eliminated. Owing to the proposed microstrip feeding structure, three resonant modes with good transmission characteristic are excited, flexibly controlled and coupled to implement a tri-mode bandpass filter. For validation, the proposed filter was designed, fabricated, and measured. Good agreement between simulation and measurement can be observed. Compared with the existing dielectric resonator filters, the proposed filter achieve good performance without the introduction of an additional accessory to suppress the radiation.

articleTitle: Design of Multifunctional Vortex Beam Antenna with Miniaturized Size
abstract: Vortex beams have opened up new areas in multiplexing communication and radar imaging, which have also sig-nicicantly improved the spectrum efficiency. At the same time, as an emerging technology, there are few studies on improving the performance of antennas that generate vortex beams, which greatly restricts its practical application. For this reason, this paper proposes a vortex beam antenna and theoretically analyzes a uniform elliptical array model that is equivalent to the characteristic currents of the antenna. Then the antenna is designed based on the proposed model and miniaturization of the antenna is achieved through the slot design. The proposed single antenna realizes the generation of two vortex beams at 5.8GHz, and the design of the feed network further realizes the mode multiplexing of the vortex beams in two directions.

articleTitle: A Broadband High-Gain Leaf-Like End-Fire Array Antenna
abstract: A broadband high-gain leaf-like end-fire array antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a long microstrip line with two ports and 2 × 16 periodical radiating elements. The microstrip line is suspended in vacuum and fed by port1. One end of the radiating element is short-circuited to the ground through a rectangular short patch, and the other end is connected to the microstrip line through a horizontal leaf-like patch. The horizontal leaf-like patch is utilized to improve the impedance matching and enhance radiation of the short patch. The proposed antenna is a leaky-wave antenna which usually have the characteristics of high gain and low profile. Using vacuum as substrate improves the bandwidth and end-fire performance of antenna. The simulated -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 32% @5.3 GHz (4.4GHz- 6.1 GHz) and gain is 14.9 dBi at 5.3 GHz, 3-dB gain bandwidth is 32% @5.3 GHz (4.1 GHz- 5.8 GHz). Eventually, the simulation results verify that the proposed design has the characteristics of broadband and high gain.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Filtenna Based on Modified Quarter-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide with High Selectivity
abstract: A compact, high-selectivity and linearly polarization (LP) patch filtenna (filtering antenna) without extra filtering circuits is presented in this paper. Two radiation nulls are introduced at both lower and upper band edges of the filter response. The proposed filtenna contains a feeding stripline, a rectangular patch, two ring patches and a modified quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) completely shielded by plated-through holes. For demonstration, an antenna prototype has been simulated, fabricated and measured. The measured results agree well with the simulated ones. According to the measured results, the antenna operates in 24.6-29.6 GHz covering the 5G N257 (26.5-29.5 GHz) and part of N258 (24.25-27.5 GHz) millimeter wave bands with reflection coefficient less than -10 dB and average gain of 5.7 dBi, which indicates that the fractional impedance bandwidth is 18.45%.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Stealth Antenna Based On Electromagnetic Bandgap
abstract: In the current complex electronic countermeasures environment, the antenna greatly restricts the performance of the aircraft. A ferrite reconfigurable stealth antenna based on electromagnetic bandgap structure is designed in this paper. By controlling the intensity or position of the bias magnetic field of the ferrite, the frequency band and pattern of the antenna can be reconstructed, and the radar cross section is reduced. Therefore, the antenna can be used in aircraft to achieve better performance.

articleTitle: The Development of Contactless In-situ Diagnostic Sensor for Additive Manufacturing using Half Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
abstract: The additive manufacturing (AM) method has gained much popularity compared to the standard production methods due to its convenience and cost-effective production; AM is also employed to fabricate passive microwave components. However, the existence of potential defects and inaccuracies has restrained its embrace in a broader application range. To date, various nondestructive procedures have been formulated, which were based on lasers, ultrasonic, and cameras, to test the quality of the fabricated component. This research discusses the development of microwave imaging techniques using half-mode substrate-integrated waveguide (HMSIW) to diagnose the presence of exposed and hidden defects in components produced using AM. The presented sensor has low-profile dimensions, making it to be utilized in-situ process monitoring and ex-situ quality testing in the realm of AM. Defects having a diameter higher than 2mm may be identified using the presented sensor.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High Gain Array Antenna for W-band Applications
abstract: In this paper, a W-band high gain array antenna with the characteristics of wide bandwidth and high gain is designed and fabricated. The radiating array and the feeding network of the antenna are designed independently. The radiating array adopts the substrate integrate cavity backed microstrip patch, which has the characteristic of wide bandwidth. The feeding network adopts the metal waveguide power divider and has the characteristic of low insertion loss. The overall aperture size of the array antenna is only 42mmx42mm. The measured results exhibit that| S11| of this array can reach −10dB from 90.5 GHz to 98.2GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 8.3%. The measured gain is larger than 30dBi from 89.0GHz to 96.5GHz with the peak gain of 31.6dBi.

articleTitle: A Metallic Miniaturized Log Periodic Dipole Array Antenna with Circular Polarization by 3D Printing
abstract: A sized-reduced log periodic dipole array antenna (LPDA) realizing circular polarization (CP) is presented. Based on the traditional LPDA principle, the crossed dipole, arranged by adding the auxiliary dipole to the inverse dipole orthogonally, is used to create the circular polarization. The proposed size-reduced CPLPKDA has 42% length reduction. The proposed antenna is fabricated by the 3D printed technology, which have advantages in the realizations of complex models. Selective laser melting (SLM), which uses aluminum alloy as material in this design, is used in fabrication. The gain of proposed antenna is 5.1 dBi over the 2.1-3.0 GHz impedance bandwidth in measurement. The proposed antenna has 73.7% impendence bandwidth (IBW) and 35.7% axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW). Radiation patterns agree well in simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Hybrid Electromagnetic Boundary for Cavity Resonance Suppression
abstract: In order to improve the traditional packaging techniques, a perfect electric conductor-perfect magnetic conductor (PEC-PMC) hybrid boundary scheme is proposed to suppress the resonant frequency of a closed metal cavity in this paper. An analytical formula of the resonant frequency of the PEC-PMC hybrid cavity is derived and then extended to cylindrical cavity with an arbitrary cross section. The simulation results indicate the accuracy of the formula. The lowest resonant frequency of the original PEC cavity is greatly increased and pushed outside of the working band by adding the PMC on its top surface. Finally, it is proposed to construct an artificial PMC boundary by covering a mushroom-type high impedance surface (HIS) on the surface of the cavity. The simulation results indicate that the mushroom can suppress the resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Profile End-fire Antenna Based on Interfinger H-type Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
abstract: This letter proposes a small-aperture and end-on-fire antenna based on spoof surface plasma polaritons (SSPPs). The antenna consists of a coplanar waveguide (CPW), a transition structure, an interfinger H-type SSPPS transmission line, and a radiating branch. The artificial surface plasmon (SPP) can bind the signal in the groove of the antenna surface, and the structure of the interfinger H -shaped transmission line has stronger field constraint ability, so that the antenna can reduce the loss. Radiant branches radiate energy into free space. The test results show that the return loss of the antenna is less than -10dB in the frequency range of 8.7~11.5 GHz, and the maximum gain can reach 10.8dBi in the frequency range of 10.4GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of D-band High Output Power Signal Sources in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Process
abstract: This paper presents two D-band (110-170 GHz) signal sources. By adopting high pass matching network in E-band (60-90 GHz) tripler and D-band doubler design, signal source I exhibits an excellent unwanted harmonics suppression of over 30 dBc. This chip achieves a measured peak output power of 5.6 dBm at 159 GHz, and the output frequency tuning range (TR) is from 143.2 to 168.8 GHz with -94 dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz phase noise. The output power of signal source II is enhanced by the adopted second harmonic output power enhancement technique in the design of D-band doubler. On wafer measurement of this chip shows a maximum output power of 7.5 dBm at 148 GHz, while the output frequency TR is between 136.8 and 156.2 GHz. Compared with other D-band signal sources, the proposed two signal sources achieve comparable frequency tuning range, phase noise and output power while using silicon-based processes.

articleTitle: A 30 MHz-2.7 GHz High-Gain Stacked-FET Power Amplifier
abstract: This paper presents a 30 MHz-2.7 GHz broadband high-gain power amplifier (PA) in 0.25 μm GaAs PHEMT technology. The fabricated two-stage PA obtains a small signal gain higher than 35.0 dB and saturated output power of 37.2±1.6 dBm from 30 MHz to 2.7 GHz, with a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 46.2% at 500 MHz. To our knowledge, this is the first report to achieve the highest gain and output power in broadband GaAs amplifier below 2.7 GHz.

articleTitle: A Modulation Recognition Algorithm of Communication Signals and Implementation Based on Digital Signal Processor
abstract: Based on the existing modulation recognition algorithms, this paper proposes a modulation recognition algorithm of communication signals based on decision tree theory by analyzing and extracting multiple signal characteristic parameters. This algorithm will find the best decision threshold by training the characteristic parameters of different signals. The research results show that the recognition accuracy of the algorithm can reach 93% when the signal noise ratio (SNR) is 10 dB, and it can recognize twelve modulation signals of CW, AM, FM, LSB, USB, 2FSK, 4FSK, BPSK, QPSK, 2ASK, 4ASK and 16QAM. The algorithm is processed in parallel on the TMS320C6678 platform to realize signal modulation identification in the frequency band of 1 to 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic energy focusing based on localized spoof surface plasmon polaritons
abstract: We propose a self-similar linear chain of several metallic spirals whose sizes and separations are decreasing proportionally. This structure owns the ability of focusing electro-mag-netic energy on subwavelength scale, with the magnitude of local electric field intensity reaching 1435, located around the smallest spiral. Near-field response spectrum and near-field mapping are performed in the microwave regime and experimental results agree well with theoretical simulation. This study may have promising applications in surface enhanced Raman scattering and elec-tromaznetic near-field sensing.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Mode-Group Beamforming System Based on An Integrated Optical True Time Delay Line Chip
abstract: An orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode-group beamforming system based on an integrated optical true time delay line (OTTDL) chip is presented in this paper. Spatial field digital modulation (SFDM) can be realized by this system. This system operating at 10.2 GHz can achieve no-distortion beam scanning, and three directions (0°, ±90°) are shown in the paper. Besides, the speed of beam scanning is measured as 1.2 kHz.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Circularly-Polarized Filtering Antenna Array with A Hybrid Feeding Network
abstract: A circularly-polarized filtering antenna array is designed in 23~27.5 GHz. Its hybrid feeding network is built up hybridly with stripline and air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) structures, for both antenna efficiency and design flexibility. The filtering response is achieved by stacked patch radiators, embedded stripline lowpass filters, the AFSIW network and a substrate integrated waveguide bandpass filter. The stripline-fed 4×4 subarrays are fabricated and measured. For the whole 16×16 array, the simulated in-band realized gain is 23.03~26.31 dBi, the out-of-band suppression is higher than 23.29 dB, and the x-polarized suppression is better than 31.13 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Continuous Mode MMIC Power Amplifiers With Bandwidth Improvement
abstract: This paper presents the design of continuous mode monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifiers (PAs) with bandwidth improvement. The output matching network (OMN) satisfying the continuous mode in broadband can be efficiently constructed with LC resonant circuits. The bandwidth can be further improved through generating the new LC unit in OMN with a minimum number of components added possible. Two prototype MMIC PAs are demonstrated with 0.25-μm Gallium Nitride (GaN) MMIC process. The measured drain efficiency is over 39.2% and 38.7% from 4.5 GHz to 6.5 GHz, respectively. When driven by 100-MHz modulated signals, two PAs exhibit great linearity performance with adjacent channel leakage ratio lower than -51.2 dBc and -53.4 dBc with digital predistortion.

articleTitle: Compact L-band Microstrip Bandpass Filters on Titanate-based Substrate
abstract: This paper presents a compact microstrip bandpass filter (BPF) for L-band wireless applications. The titanate-based substrate with a high dielectric constant of 135 is used to reduce the size of the BPF that is fabricated by the thin film process. The Miniaturization leads to multiple cross coupling effects, which introduces out-of-band transmission zeros. The L-band microstrip BPF has been designed, fabricated and tested, which has a small size of 3.2×5×0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The simulated and measured results show that two transmission zeros locate at the both sides of the passband and the insertion loss of the BPF is less than 2.5 dB at central frequency while the out-of-band suppression is more than 50 dB.

articleTitle: A Dual-Frequency Microwave Rectifier Circuit for Microwave Power Transmission
abstract: In this paper, a dual-frequency rectifier circuit with high conversion efficiency is proposed for microwave power transmission (MPT). The Class-F load structure is adopted in the harmonic suppression network. In order to determine the input power and load resistance, the impedance matching network is optimized by source-pull simulation. Experimental results show that, with an input power of 14.8 dBm, the peak conversion efficiencies at 3.5 and 5.8 GHz can reach 72.81 % and 73.44%, respectively. And the proposed rectifier circuit has a superior performance in circuit area and design cost.

articleTitle: Deep-learning based noise-resistant broadband signal recovery for fiber-connected radar networks
abstract: A deep learning based broadband radar signal recovery method for fiber-connected radar networks is proposed, which is implemented by using a residual convolutional neural network (RCNN) to deal with the defects of analog fiber transmission systems. In order to enhance the robustness of the proposed scheme, a method for training the network with data superimposed with extra noise is also demonstrated, based on which the RCNN is able to compensate for the nonlinear spurs, noises, and signal distortions in low-noise conditions. In the experiment, signal recovery of 3-GHz bandwidth radar echoes after 8-km fiber transmission is realized with the average mean square error (MSE) of the waveforms reduced by ~19 dB, and the dynamic range for maintaining a good pulse compression performance is increased by 35 dB.

articleTitle: Multilayered Lossy -Bandstop- Filter- Based Negative-Group- Delay RF Circuit With Broadband Input-Reflectionless Behavior
abstract: A multilayered lossy-bandstop-filter-(BSF)-based negative-group-delay (NGD) RF circuit with wide-band input-reflectionless behavior is presented. It is designed by using a los-sy-complementary-diplexer-based topology, in which the NGD circuit is built with a microstrip lossy-BSF network printed on the top layer, whilst a resistively-terminated lossy vertical transition is exploited to absorb the reflected RF -input-signal energy to attain perfect matching at the center frequency to and broadband input-quasi-reflectionless behavior. The RF operational principle of the devised NGD circuit is detailed and its properties in terms of NGD profile and power-attenuation responses are graphically discussed. As practical validation, a two-layered microstrip-lossy-BSF -based NGD circuit prototype is developed and measured with power-attenuation level of 19.62 dB and NGD depth of −0.82 ns at 0.996 GHz, NGD bandwidth of 417 MHz (i.e., 41.8%), and input-power-matching levels above 9.18 dB from DC to 2.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz Millimeter-wave Antenna Based on Highly Conductive Graphene-assembled Films
abstract: In this paper, a 60 GHz millimeter-wave antenna based on highly conductive graphene-assembled films is proposed for wireless communications. The proposed antenna is designed with microstrip line discontinuities radiation and made of the gra-phene-assembled film with conductivity of 1.1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> S/m by laser engraving method. The proposed antenna possesses some significant advantages of compact structure, low profile and high gain. The simulated and measured results show that the antenna has a high gain of 12.2 dBi at 60 GHz, and a satisfying return loss of -40 dB.

articleTitle: Combining Wireless Backscatter and Power for Future IoSP
abstract: In this paper we show how to combine Wireless Power and Backscatter Communications to deploy extremely low power sensors for the implementation of future Internet of things and Internet of Space Probes, that could be used to sense and evaluate interplanetary bodies. This includes Mars and Moon base approaches.

articleTitle: One-bit Quantization SAR imaging using Phaseless Measurements
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) theory has achieved signifificant success in the field of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. Recent studies have shown that SAR imaging for sparse scene can also be successfully performed with one-bit quantized data. Many algorithms were proposed for one-bit SAR imaging. These algorithms can recover data only if the sensing matrix is accurate. But when the SAR system contains phase error (i.e., the sensing matrix has error), the SAR image recovered by these classical algorithms will defocus. In this work, We introduce a novel framework where phaseless transformation is adopted to realize autofocus in one-bit SAR imaging. The proposed method has excellent focusing ability and reduces hardware cost appropriately. The simulation results of the point targets and extended targets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Compact Quad-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dual-Band Filter With Controllable Frequency
abstract: In this article, a compact dual-band bandpass filter based on quad-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonators with controllable frequency is proposed. The bandwidth of the filter can be adjusted by changing the position and angle of the metallized vias in the SIW resonant cavity. The X-shaped slot on the resonant cavity extends the transmission path of the surface current, which can realize the controllability of the filter frequency.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency On-Chip Measurement System for Millimeter Wave/Terahertz High-Resolution Phase Shifter
abstract: The frequency response of phase shifter could be measured with the help of the vector network analyzer (VNA). But such a method suffers low efficiency when we need to measure millimeter wave (mmWave)/terahertz high-resolution phase shifter, because the operation states of the phase shifter would increase exponentially as the resolution increases, implying longer measurement time. To confront the challenge, in this paper, a high-efficiency on-chip measurement system for the mm Wave/terahertz high-resolution phase shifter is proposed. Based on the VNA and the probe station, we develop a multifunction platform to automatically change the operation state of the under-test phase shifter, and construct the coding to render the PC to control the measurement process. With the utilization of the proposed measurement system, we could finish the measurement of mm Wave/terahertz high-resolution phase shifter in a significantly shorter time.

articleTitle: Application for spatial ASK modulation in UHF RFID transmitter based on digital metamaterial
abstract: The incompatibility of the cost and performance is a restrictive factor for the further development of RFID. In this paper, combining the latest development of digital metamaterial and RFID technology, a UHF RFID transmitter with spatial ASK modulation is proposed to reduce the complexity and the cost of radio frequency communication system equipment. The 1-bit digital metamaterial units based on polarization-insensitive Jerusalem cross structure form the 10×10 coding matrix. The proposed UHF RFID transmitter based on digital metamaterial inno-vatively realizes the spatial ASK modulation from -60° to 60° in azimuth plane. Finally, a preliminary communication system is built to test the performance of transmitter. The test result shows that the modulation depth of the spatial UHF RFID transmitter are all above 75%. The transmitter based on spatial ASK modulation provide a potential ability to solve the problem of missing tags in RFID system.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparison of window functions based on arch measurement system
abstract: In this paper, the method of eliminating the interference signals of the arch measurement system is investigated deeply according to IEEE STD1128 1998. Based on the time domain signals converted from the frequency domain data simulated in Microwave Studio CST, the interference signals, such as self-coupling energy, spurious coupling energy, and multiple reflection energy are discussed. Several different window functions are presented and compared to eliminate the interference signals in time domain, so as to increase the accuracy of arch measurement system.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Compact Power Divider Based on Micro-coaxial Lines
abstract: This paper presents a compact four-way power divider based on micro-coaxial lines. For ease of testing, two of the same power dividers are placed back-to-back, and CPW to micro-coaxial Line transitions are added to input/output ports. The whole structure is directly measured on wafer using a probe system. In W band, the measured return loss is greater than 15 dB and the insertion loss is smaller than 1.3 dB.

articleTitle: Quad-Band Impedance Transformer for Extremely High Load Impedance Matching with Out-of-Band Spurious Response Suppression
abstract: A novel approach to design a quad-band impedance transformer (QBIT) is presented. The primary purpose of this transformer is to match an extremely high load impedance to a source impedance of 50Ω at four distinct frequency bands with suppression of the spurious passband. The proposed QBIT is constructed using a π-shaped topology and two series microstrip-lines. The ABCD matrix method is employed to derive closed-form design formulas. The latter are employed to obtain the circuit parameters that allow for matching extremely high load impedances. For validation, two prototypes of QBIT realized to match 500Ω and 1500Ω loads are fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured transformer characteristics are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A Folded Planar Luneburg Lens for Multi-Beams Antennas Application
abstract: This paper presents a two-dimensional compact Luneburg lens operating in X-band for beamforming network (BFN) application. The Luneburg lens is realized by drilling holes in a double-layers substrate, and to reduce the size of lens, it is folded into a half-cylinder. Compared with previous planar lens design, the proposed Luneburg lens's profile is reduced by half while maintaining good performance. The proposed BFN can provide a phase scanning range of about ±95° by switching the feeding port. The experiments show that the design can achieve a 10% bandwidth for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10dB at 10 GHz. Measured and simulated results agree well.

articleTitle: A Fans-Shaped Beam Antenna Design for Overcoming Multipath Effects for 77GHz FMCW-MIMO Radar
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain and Fans-Shaped Beam (FSB) antenna is designed. It is used as the array element of a Multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) radar with 192 virtual channels. Measurement result shows that the antenna can improve its radar imaging performance due to its enhanced ability to overcome multipath effects caused by reflection of ground, which can be understood by the principle of MIMO radar.

articleTitle: A D-Band I/Q Drain Mixer for Direct Up-convertion in 70-nm GaAs Technology
abstract: An I/Q up-conversion MMIC that works in the D-band with the 70nm mHEMT GaAs process is designed in this paper, using a transistor drain mixing unit. The mixer can maintain good performance in the 125-155 GHz frequency band. Without adding any pre- or post-amplifier, the measured conversion gain is -8 dB, the input IF bandwidth exceeds 10 GHz and the isolation between ports is greater than 20 dB. It maintains good linearity under the IF input power of less than 2dBm. The performance parameters of this upconverter are predominant among the GaAs mHEMT-based mixers reported in this frequency band.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Regularized Subspace Pursuit based Variable Step-size Method for Power Amplifier Sparse Model Selection
abstract: A novel Adaptive Regularized Subspace Pursuit based Variable Step-size (ARSP-VS) algorithm is proposed for power amplifier (PA) and digital predistorters(DPD) modeling. Experiments were performed on a test platform of a Class AB PA driven by a 20-MHz LTE signal and a 4-carrier 80M LTE signal. The results show that the proposed algorithm has better linearization performance than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Filtering Antenna Based on Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide
abstract: This paper presents a novel circularly polarized (CP) filtering antenna based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW). Circularly polarized wave radiation is obtained by etching irregular slots on the ISGW transmission waveguide to form perturbation, and filtering is introduced by interdigital coupling line feed on the ISGW transmission line. The simulation results show that the CP filtering antenna has a center frequency of 31 GHz, and |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB from 25.5 to 36.4 GHz, i.e., a relative bandwidth of 35.06%. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 27.7-30.8 GHz, i.e., a relative axial ratio bandwidth of 10%. The antenna gain in the 3-dB AR bandwidth range is greater than 6.2 dBi, and the out-of-band suppression is above 14.4 dB.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Broadband Amplifier Design Methodology in Silicon-Based Technology
abstract: In the mm-wave frequency bands, there are more frequency specturm resources compared to the sub-6 frequency band. From 10 GHz to 40 GHz, it covers K/Ka-band wireless communication applications, such as car radar application and mm-wave 5G application. Those applications also easily occupy GHz bandwidth for high data rate communication. In this work, the design methodology of a broadband application in the mmwave frequency is presented, and an mm-wave low noise amplifier is provided as a design case in a SiGe technology with more than 90% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Efficient Pruning Method of Digital Predistortion Suitable for Power Amplifiers with Scalable Output Power
abstract: In this paper, a new pruning method of digital predistortion based on optimal brain surgeon (OBS) algorithm is proposed, which reduces the algorithm complexity significantly in power scalable applications. The conventional OBS algorithm is modified for complex value DPD application by pruning the redundant items according to their impact on model accuracy such as normalized mean squared error (NMSE). Compared to conventional DPD, more than 60% of the coefficients can be reduced almost without obvious performance degradation.

articleTitle: A Bayesian Approach for Estimating Heart Rate using FMCW Radar
abstract: This paper illustrates a Markov model of peak-finding and gives a Bayesian method for estimating heart rate based on an FMCW radar. The Bayesian method provides a framework for estimation and inference and noise peaks can be filtered out. Conjugate priors are used making the algorithm computation-ef-ficient. A real-time algorithm is given and several experiments have been carried out. It is shown that the accuracy of the heart rate is close to reference and much more stable than the traditional FFT method and promising in overcoming noise.

articleTitle: Unknown Interference Source Positioning Based on Near-Field Scanning
abstract: The positioning of electromagnetic interference (EMI) sources is of high importance in electromagnetic compatibility applications. In this paper, a method for interference source positioning based on near-field scanning is proposed. Known reference sources and the unknown device under test(DUT) are placed between shielding planes. Due to the multi patches effect, the radiated near-fields from the DUT only shows larger correlation with that from the reference source very close to the DUT. According to this, by scanning the electric near-field around the shielding planes and calculating the correlation coefficients, the position of the DUT can be estimated. The proposed method is validated by simulations examples, and both a single interference source and two interference sources can be predicted. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method can be used in interference source positioning.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Millimeter Wave Antenna with Enhanced Port Isolation Based on LTCC Technology for 5G Applications
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized millimeter wave antenna with enhanced port isolation based on LTCC technology for 5G applications. In order to achieve higher isolation, metal vias are added to the original antenna structure. The two polarizations are excited by two vertical feeding lines below. This antenna is designed and manufactured based on low-temperature co-fire ceramic (LTCC) technology for ease of integration. The simulated results show that the antenna have -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 25.8-27 GHz, and port isolation is higher than 17 dB. When compared with the dual-polarized antenna without metal vias, the proposed antenna shows the higher isolation in the frequency band. The proposed antenna is suitable for integration and 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Ridge Waveguide Four-port Junction Circulator
abstract: This paper presents a compact ridge waveguide four-port junction circulator. It adopts a parallel configuration topology of two 3-port ridge waveguide junction circulators connected with a compact ridge waveguide to coaxial transition. The compactness of the circulator are realized by selection of ridge waveguide transmission line, utilization of parallel configuration topology structure and compact transition form. Low-power and high-power test results demonstrate that this circulator realizes a 17 dB isolation and 24 dB return loss bandwidth of 11.8% with an insertion loss of 0.2-0.4 dB. Its peak power capacity can reach 8 kW.

articleTitle: A Low Amplitude/Phase Error 16dB CMOS Variable Gain Amplifier with 180° Phase Shifting
abstract: This paper demonstrates A CMOS independent cascode current cancelling (ICCC) variable gain amplifier (VGA) which achieves 16dB gain variation and 180° phase shift. Under different gain states, only a 1.6° phase error and a 0.2dB gain error can be found from 15 GHz to 25 GHz in 40-nm CMOS without any calibration by eliminating the effect of parasitic capacitors in off-state. Owing to the cascode structure, the peak gain of the VGA is 12dB with only one stage including input/output pads. Besides, the VGA can also serve as a 180° phase shift (PS) with no more than 1.5° phase error and 0.2dB gain error. In addition, the S11 and S22 keep almost unchanged with gain/phase variations. The measured −3-dB bandwidth is 5 GHz and OP1dB is 0.3dBm in the maximum gain state. The VGA consumes 16mW power from 1.1V voltage. The area is 0.065mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding input/output pads.

articleTitle: A 22–34 GHz Wide-Band Low Noise Amplifier with 22 dB Gain and 4 dB NF
abstract: This paper presents a wide-band two-stage low noise amplifier (LNA) with about 12 GHz 3-dB-bandwidth, covering the 26/28 GHz 5G millimeter-wave band. Neutralization technique is utilized in both two common-source stages to improve the entire performance include noise figure (NF), gain and stability. By tuning the transistor biasing voltage, the amplifier gain is changed by 6 dB. The measured peak gain and noise figure is 22 dB and 4 dB, respectively. With the gate-source coupling technique, a broadband input matching bandwidth is achieved with better than 10 dB return loss in the operating frequency. At 28 GHz, the measured output 1-dB compression point (OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>) is up to 2.8 dBm.

articleTitle: A 45 GHz Low-Voltage Cascode Power Amplifier Based on Capacitor Coupling Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a low-voltage cascode (CC) power amplifier (PA) for IEEE 802.11aj (45 GHz) application. A capacitor coupling technology is employed to adapt the CC PA to low-voltage systems. By deploying an asymmetrical capacitor to the balun, the maximum phase unbalance is suppressed from 1.7° to 0.2°. For the proof of concept, a low-voltage CC PA was fabricated in a 0.13-µm SiGe BiCMOS technology with a core size of 0.93×0.53 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Measurements for 1.5-V VDD show that, at 42-/44-/46-/48-GHz, the PA achieves 14.8-/14.6-/14.5-/14.6-dBm output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB). In the frequency band of 6.5 GHz from 42 to 48.5 GHz, the small-signal gain is 27.5-29.5 dB, and the S22/S11 is better than −9.5/−10.5 dB.

articleTitle: Development and preliminary experimental results of novel three-band multi-polarization airborne SAR system
abstract: Compared with traditional single-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, the multi-band, multi-polarization SAR system can obtain more observation information to improve the ability of targets recognition, and becomes an important research direction. Therefore, we developed a new highly integrated airborne three-band multi-polarization SAR system, which works in low/medium/high (L/X/Ka band) frequency, and has the ability of full-polarity. Three-band phased array antennas are integrated a whole coplanar structure, and controlled by one task management unit. Each band of the system can work alone or together at the basis frequency and basis time, to obtain different frequency SAR images of the same area simultaneously. The results of flight experiments verify the function and performance of the system effectively. The design and application of this SAR system is significant for quantitative remote sensing observation and instructive for future radar system development.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Extension Techniques for CMOS Low-Noise Amplifiers
abstract: Wideband low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) are extensively employed in various systems such as software-defined radio (SDR), multi-mode transceivers, and high-speed links. However, gain-bandwidth products are quite limited as operation frequencies approach f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>. This paper introduces some bandwidth extension design techniques for millimeter-wave and terahertz LNAs in CMOS technologies. Stagger tuning technique of multi-stage LNA, transformer-based matching network and pole-control technique with transformer feedback are discussed and compared.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with Flat Gain for RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: A miniaturized Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA) with flat gain is proposed in this paper for UWB applications. This antenna is implemented by loading a pair of open stubs, comb-shaped slot array, and semi-elliptical patches on a traditional AVA. The miniaturization property is obtained as a result of the introduction of comb-shaped slits which increases the surface current path. The function of the pair of open stubs is to improve the gain in the lower frequency band, while the effect of the pair of semi-elliptical patches is to maintain the gain in the higher frequency band. In order to verify this design concept, a prototype of the proposed AVA is fabricated and measured. The measured results show that VSWR <; 2 in the frequency band of 3 - 11GHz and the average gain in is 8.9 dBi in the end-fire direction. Besides the gain fluctuation is ± 1.1dB within this impedance bandwidth, achieving a relatively flat gain.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Capture and Tracking Algorithm Based on Spread Spectrum Communication
abstract: In the missile-borne communication system, the mis-sile-borne target is in a highly dynamic environment. This paper uses direct sequence spread spectrum to adopt large frequency offset acquisition and high-dynamic tracking algorithms for high-speed moving targets to realize the communication between the missile-borne target and the ground control system. The large frequency offset capture algorithm captures the target signal by designing a matched filter, in which the filter coefficient is consistent with the equalized GOLD code used by the target. A high dynamic tracking loop is used to realize real-time tracking processing for the remaining frequency offset and the real-time speed change of the target after capture. The tracking loop is composed of a phase detector, a loop filter, and a local frequency oscillator. This paper designs the FPGA implementation method of the capture and tracking algorithm, and verifies the performance of the algorithm throgh simulation and hardware testing.

articleTitle: Bandpass Filter Inspired Filtering Patch Antenna
abstract: A planar filtering patch antenna inspired by BPF (bandpass filter) prototype is proposed in this paper. The antenna has a very simple structure, while realizing multifunctional operation, including directional radiation and filtering functions. The principle of replacing the LC resonator of BPF prototype with a patch resonator is illustrated. The newly obtained prototype is displayed in the physical form of a patch antenna fed by a differential coupled line. A microstrip-to-slotline transition is introduced to generate the differential signal. As a result, the proposed antenna achieves good filtering response with two radiation nulls on the two sides of the passband. The measured results agree well with simulation.

articleTitle: Broadband Metasurface Antenna with Low Cross-polarization Based on Characteristic Theory
abstract: In this paper, a design method of a broadband metasurface antenna with low cross-polarization based on characteristic theory is presented. Firstly, the mode field distribution of the metasurface is analyzed, and multiple specific characteristic modes are effectively excited through the magnetic current gap. Then the appropriate characteristic mode is selected to form a broadband radiation metasurface antenna. This design solves the inherent problems of high Q, high insertion loss and narrow frequency band of traditional microstrip antennas.

articleTitle: Metallic Micro-Machined Corrugated Conical Horn Antenna in the 500–750 GHz Band
abstract: In this paper, a terahertz (THz) corrugated conical horn antenna based on metallic micro-machining technology is proposed. The horn is composed of 21 copper layers. Each copper layer is used the low speed wire cut technology to form the desired structure. The horn reveals a bandwidth of VSWR < 2 from 500 to 750 GHz. The simulated radiation patterns exhibit symmetric gaussian beams with low sidelobe level. The antenna gain varies from 18.3 to 20.1 dBi and the good gaussicity above 95% is achieved in the whole band.

articleTitle: An improved Model and Estimation Method for Delay/Doppler Altimetry
abstract: Semi-analytical model for the echo of spaceborne delay/Doppler altimetry (DDA) has been proved efficient and meaningful. However, the complexity of motion errors could not be neglected in low-altitude and highly maneuver flight, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) remote sensing. At the beginning of this paper, an improved expression for the flat surface impulse response (FSIR) considering vertical motion errors is proposed. The formulation, being one term of the mean echo power, allows for an explicit understanding of how the various vertical position and slight movement affect the waveform. Then a convolution neural network (CNN) is utilized to classify the objects in quantities which are detected in the first step. Simulated results on a set of delay Doppler maps (DDMs) demonstrate that the proposed method is able to generate desirable description of the scene.

articleTitle: A High-Temperature-Resistant Frequency Selective Rasorber with Low-Frequency Diffusion and High-Frequency Transmission
abstract: A frequency selective rasober (FSR) with high-temperature-resistance, wideband radar cross section reduction (RCSR), and flat-broad transmission band is presented in this paper. It consists of three functional layers: a piece of insulation tile, scattering cancellation metasurface based on interdigitated element, and a triple-layer-coupled-resonator spatial filter frequency selective surface. At low-frequency band, the incident energy is diffused to various directions, resulting in 10 dB RCSR over 2.52-11.68 GHz with a 129% fractional bandwidth. Besides, there is a highly efficient transmission band (insertion loss < 0.595 dB) over 16.53-19.83 GHz. It is also worth mentioning that our FSR can maintain such good properties at 500°C for 5 seconds with the help of insulation tile.

articleTitle: A Broad-band Dual Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna with Low Profile
abstract: A broadband dual circularly polarized microstrip antenna with low profile is presented. The profile of the antenna is reduced by directly etching the patch antenna on the substrate block, and the circular polarization direction can be changed in a wide frequency band by feeding the antenna with 3dB bridge network. The proposed antenna has 51.0% impedance bandwidth (VSWR <; 2) and 33.4% circularly polarized axial ratio bandwidth (AR <; 3 dB). The final profile of the antenna is only 0.17 λ, and has good circular polarization radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Validation of Highly Compact Branch-Line Balun For Quad-Band Applications
abstract: In this communication, a novel design approach to design of highly compact quad-band branch-line balun (BLB) is presented along with the implementation and experimental validation of the structure. A quad-band transmission-line is obtained by adding one coupled-line between two-series transmission-lines used to replace the traditional 90° microstrip-lines of a single-band BLB. The even/odd-mode technique is employed to derive the closed-form formulas and facilitate the analysis of the quad-band properties. The proposed concept is verified through fabrication and measurements of a quad-band BLB operating at 1.0, 2.7, 4.1 and 5.8 GHz. The manufactured quad-band BLB provides a reflection coefficient better than -20dB with a magnitude imbalance smaller than 0.45dB. Furthermore, the fabricated prototype (0.051λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) exhibits a size reduction of 59.2% and 84.9% when compared to a single-band balun (0.125λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and the recent quad-band BLB (0.336λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) reported in the literature, respectively.

articleTitle: A New Method for Measuring Calibration Factors of Microwave Power Transfer Standard
abstract: Power is the fundamental parameter among the radio frequency metrology key parameters, which provides the traceability to many parameters. To ensure the preciseness of power measurement, accurate expression and analysis of calibration factor is indispensable. In conventional method, calibration factor of power sensor and adapter combination is based on efficiency equation. Measurement uncertainty is relatively large due to network analyzer's uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a novel approach calculating calibration factor of combination, based on transmission line's loss factor. Measurement uncertainty is expected to decrease from 3% to 2%, with novel approach applied. Calculation method is proved by calibration experiment of 7mm power transfer standard. Difference of calibration factor between calculation and experiment is reduced by 75%, indicating a dramatical decrease of measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Kalman Filter based Digital Phase Detector for All Digital Phase-Locked Loop
abstract: This work proposes an adaptive Kalman filter (AKF) based digital phase detector that compresses the phase detector's (PD) output noise in all-digital phase locked loop (ADPLL). The ADPLL is modeled mathematically and the noise sources are extracted. An AKF is designed based on the ADPLL model and is inserted after the PD to optimize its output noise. This AKF takes the advantage of the statistical properties of the noise and adapt its parameter to make itself an optimal filter. Simulation is done in MATLAB and the result reveals the correctness and stability of the design. The PD gets a 16.9 dB noise power decrease in the simulation.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Microstrip Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: The proposed antenna is a multiband and broadband microstrip antenna. The research will focus on incorporating UWB including GSM, UMTS, 4G/5G and ISM bands with more efficient antenna performance. The antenna gain can reach 3.31dB at 4.8GHz and the antenna efficiency is more than 94%. In addition, the 2 × 2 array is studied. To fabricate a complete energy harvesting system, we design a 1-4 Wilkinson power divider, a suitable matching network and a rectification circuit. Finally, an integrated energy harvesting system is fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Array Antenna Synthesis With Cross-Polarization Suppression Via Convex Optimization
abstract: The paper focuses on the problem of suppressing the cross-polarization level (XPL) when simultaneously receiving orthogonal polarization signal from different directions with a wide-beam common aperture array antenna. The polarizations are the the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and the lefthand circular polarization (LHCP). The paper firstly sets up a non convex optimization problem and then converts it into a series of convex problems. An iterative algorithm is designed to solve the new convex problems, in which two tuning parameters are utilized to guarantee the convergence. With the proposed scheme, the XPL in the LHCP (RHCP) signal direction for the RHCP (LHCP) receiving could be suppressed to the desired level. In addition, the designed scheme can be easily extended to optimize the mainlobe ripple level (MRL) and the sizelobe level (SLL) with a simply derivation.

articleTitle: Efficient Inverse Covariance Matrix Estimation for Low-Complexity Closed-Loop DPD Systems
abstract: This paper studies closed-loop digital predistortion systems, with special focus on linearization of mmW active antenna arrays. Considering the beam-dependent nonlinear distortion and very high DPD processing rates, a modified self-orthogonalized (SO) learning solution is proposed, which is capable of reducing the computational complexity compared to other similar solutions, while at the same time obtaining a comparable linearization performance. The modified SO consists of a novel method for efficiently calculating the inverse of the input data covariance matrix. Thorough RF measurement results at 28 GHz band featuring a state-of-the-art 64 element active array and channel bandwidths up to 800 MHz, are reported. A complexity analysis is also carried out which, together with the obtained results, allow to asses the performance-complexity trade-offs. Altogether, the results show that the proposed methods can facilitate efficient mmW active antenna array linearization.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of a New 2.4mm Coaxial Microcalorimeter
abstract: A new structure of coaxial microcalorimeter system in 2.4mm coaxial connector is introduced in this paper for metrological purpose, working as primary standard for coaxial radio-frequency (RF) power sensor calibration up to 50 GHz. Proposed apparatus allows direct calibration of the commercial thermoelectric power sensors. Hence assembly procedure is simplified for future calibration service, and traceability chain is shortened as well. Instead of conventional microcalorimeter using thermistor mount as DUT (Device Under Test), proposed microcalorimeter system applies thermoelectric power sensor as DUT which has lower mismatch error, wider working frequency band from 50GHz down to DC and more stable than thermistor mount when working as transfer standard. Eventually, measurement uncertainty is expected to be obviously reduced than thermistor mount.

articleTitle: A Low Amplitude/Phase Error 16dB CMOS Variable Gain Amplifier with 180° Phase Shifting
abstract: This paper demonstrates A CMOS independent cascode current cancelling (ICCC) variable gain amplifier (VGA) which achieves 16dB gain variation and 180° phase shift. Under different gain states, only a 1.6° phase error and a 0.2dB gain error can be found from 15 GHz to 25 GHz in 40-nm CMOS without any calibration by eliminating the effect of parasitic capacitors in off-state. Owing to the cascode structure, the peak gain of the VGA is 12dB with only one stage including input/output pads. Besides, the VGA can also serve as a 180° phase shift (PS) with no more than 1.5° phase error and 0.2dB gain error. In addition, the S11 and S22 keep almost unchanged with gain/phase variations. The measured −3-dB bandwidth is 5 GHz and OP1dB is 0.3dBm in the maximum gain state. The VGA consumes 16mWpower from 1.1V voltage. The area is 0.065mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding input/output pads.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Luzzatto Power Divider with Second and Third Harmonic Suppression Using Open Stubs
abstract: A miniaturized three-way Luzzatto power divider with second and third harmonic suppression is presented in this paper. In this proposed structure, the quarter-wavelength microstrip lines are replaced with T-shaped structures for harmonic suppression and miniaturization, while the half-wavelength microstrip lines are shortened by adding several open stubs. The proposed structure achieves suppression of more than 14.2 dB at second harmonic and 24.4 dB at third harmonic within the 1 dB bandwidth, while the circuit size is reduced to 1/4 compared with conventional Luzzatto divider. Measurement and simulation results are in good agreements under the fundamental frequency of 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A Portable 5.8 GHz Radar Sensor with an Integreted Common-Aperture Single Antenna for Noncontact Physiological Monitoring
abstract: In this paper, a portable 5.8 GHz Doppler radar with an integrated common aperture single antenna is proposed for noncontact monitoring of physiological signals such as respiration and heartbeat. The conventional Doppler radar system usually employs two separate transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) antennas for improved Tx/Rx isolation. However, it inevitably adds up to the size of the radar system. By leveraging the characteristics of the rat-race coupler, a common-aperture antenna was designed and integrated together with the radar transceiver on a single printed circuit board (PCB), which dramatically reduces the size of the entire radar system. The proposed antenna's Tx/Rx isolation at 5.8 GHz is measured to be higher than 35 dB. Compared with the conventional two separate antennas with similar isolation, the size of the proposed single antenna is reduced by 160% and the entire radar system is reduced in area by 80% with a size of only 10 cm×5 cm. Experiments were carried out in the office environment to wirelessly detect human vital signs. It was demonstrated that the proposed portable radar system integrated with a com-mon-aperture single antenna can successfully capture the physio-lozlcal signals of respiration and heartbeat.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna and Array with Stacked Structure
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized (CP) antenna for millimeter wave (mmWave) communications is proposed. The antenna is fed by a microstrip line and the energy is coupled through a slot in the middle layer to excite the driven patch and radiation patch on the top layer. The slot is rotated with an angle to generate the CP waves. Based on the CP antenna element, a 4×4 array with full-corporate feeding network is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the -10 dB impedance bandwidth is covered from 22 to 30 GHz, the relative impedance bandwidth exceeds 30.7%, and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 22.2% is from 22 to 27.5 GHz. The CP array antenna is a good candidate for mmWave fifth generation (5G) mobile communications.

articleTitle: High Isolation Compact Base Station Array Antenna Using Decoupled Surface and Parasitic Patch Structure
abstract: In this paper, a dual polarized cross dipole antenna for base station is designed. There is a severe mutual coupling between the compact antenna units. By adding a decoupled surface and parasitic patch structure, the isolation of the co-polarization and cross-polarization can be significantly improved. With the decoupled surface, the co-polarization isolation between adjacent units is increased from 14dB to 20dB, and the cross-polarization isolation between adjacent units is improved from 10dB to 22.5dB during 3.3-3.6GHz band. Besides, the isolation between two ports of the same unit is better than 25dB.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in EM-Centric Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization
abstract: Multiphysics analysis is important for high performance RF/microwave component and system design. For effective device analysis, it is crucial to understand the relationships of different physical domains. This article gives a review of the recent progress in multiphysics parametric modeling exploiting space-mapping-based approach and multiphysics optimization using advanced transfer function surrogate model. To demonstrate these methods, two microwave filter applications are used.

articleTitle: Tunable First-Order Balanced Filter with Reflectionless Characteristics for Both Common- and Differential- Mode Signals
abstract: This work presents a novel tunable first-order absorptive balanced filter. It consists of a coupled-line bandpass filter with absorption networks connected at its input and output ports. The absorption network is designed using semi-lumped elements. With the proposed architecture, reflectionless performance can be achieved for both the common-mode (CM) noise and out-of-band differential-mode (DM) signal. Besides, the circuit is compact by nature due to the use of semi-lumped elements. To demonstrate the proposed idea, a microstrip prototype is fabricated and measured. The measured results show excellent reflectionless performance for both CM noise and DM signal. The measured DM transmission loss varies from 3.7dB to 2.2dB within a frequency tuning range of 1.6GHz-1.9GHz. Meanwhile, the DM reflection coefficient is lower than −9.5dB from 0.1 GHz-5.6GHz. The CM reflection coefficient is lower than −10dB while the circuit still exhibits suppression higher than 22dB for the transmission of CM noise from 0.1GHz-2.3GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Polarized Filtering Metasurface Antenna for 5G Applications
abstract: This manuscript presents a new broadband ±45° dual-polarized filtering metasurface antenna using low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process for 5G application. By adopting the four metasurface units excited by a cross-type slot and etching the slot on the metasurface, the antenna can introduce two upper-band-edge radiation nulls to realize a good upper stopband suppression with a high level of 30dB. Meanwhile, four horizontal strips connected with four grounding probes are loaded below the metasurface to produce a lower-band- edge null, achieving the lower stop band. As a result, a good dual-polarized filtering patch antenna is constructed with a wide operating frequency band of 24.6-29.4GHz (18.4%) and good stopband suppression for both two polarizations, as well as high polarization isolation of 25dB. The average in-band gain is about 5.8dB and the average efficiency in the band is over 90%, moreover, the efficiency at upper/lower stopband can be suppressed to be almost less than 5%.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Dual-Polarized Micro-Lens Antenna
abstract: A 320GHz dual-polarized micro-lens antenna based on orthomode transducer(OMT) is proposed for focal plane array. The designed micro-lens antenna features two polarization ports, the leaky wave structure and the OMT. The return loss of both ports is better than -15dB from 305 to 326GHz. The isolation between the two ports is greater than 80 dB. The gain of this antenna is 20.3dBi and 20.2dBi for vertical polarization and horizontal polarization, respectively. The half-power beam width (HPBW) is 18.05°, and the sidelobe level is lower than -20dB.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a 20-kW Injection-locked Magnetron with Load-Pull Characterization
abstract: A 20-kW S-band injection-locked magnetron with load-pull characterization system was actual test and verify. By searching the optimal load of the magnetrons, the performances of corresponding system could be improved. An enhanced injection-locked bandwidth, a low injection power and a preferable output phase noise performances were achieved. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is one of the lowest injection power (3W) and highest phase noise performances (-85 dBc/Hz@50 kHz) ever reported for an S-band injection-locked magnetron with a power output of over 20 kW.

articleTitle: Design of a Millimeter-wave Slotted Array Antenna with Miniaturized Dimension and Low Side-lobes
abstract: A W -band slot array antenna with low side lobes, fed by a ridge waveguide, is presented in this paper for the applications with strict dimensional limitation. A 94 GHz slotted array antenna was simulated using finite element modeling (FEM) in HFSS. The feed network is analyzed by the equivalent circuit method, and the analysis of side lobe level was based on Taylor distribution. Compared with the theoretical calculations, the simulation results exhibit an excellent performance with high gain of 32 dB and low sidelobes level of -22.9 dB. And the size of this antenna is reduced to 45 % of that of standard waveguide WR10 in the cross-section. It is a promising solution to apply in millimeter wave for high Integration module.

articleTitle: A Compact 1.71-2.69GHz Diplexer Based on HRS IPD Technology
abstract: In this paper, a compact 1.71-2.69GHz diplexer is designed and fabricated for mobile phone terminals based on high-resistivity silicon (HRS) integrated passive device (IPD) technology. Low insertion loss and compact size can be achieved by utilizing new LC resonances to provide transmission zeros. The chip size of the diplexer is 1.525mm×0.95mm×0.1mm. Test results show that the operating center frequencies of the low and high frequency bands of the diplexer are 1.94 GHz and 2.595 GHz, respectively. The low band maximum insertion loss is 1.3dB in 1.71GHz ~ 2.17GHz. The high band maximum insertion loss is 0.7dB in 2.5GHz ~ 2.69GHz. The isolation between two bands is better than 11.2dB in 1.71GHz ~ 2.69GHz.

articleTitle: Implementation and Design of Signal Pre-Processing System Based on Interference Source Detective Device
abstract: Radio interference source detective technology plays an important role in aerospace, daily activities and mobile communication domains. In this paper, we introduce a signal preprocessing system based on interference source detective device, it has the ability to monitor and identify navigation interference signals. The whole system mainly uses FPGA chip, which has high flexibility and is also successfully used on actual hardware platforms.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of EPC-MIMO radar for range ambiguity resolution
abstract: The range ambiguity poses a challenge in radar systems. To solve this problem, the element-pulse coding (EPC) scheme is performed in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. In this paper, the signal-to-ambiguous-plus-noise ratio (SANR) is introduced to evaluate the range ambiguity resolvability of the EPC-MIMO radar, where targets in different range regions can be separated effectively through conventional beamforming algorithm under ideal conditions. Moreover, under the DOA mismatch and amplitude-phase error, two methods are developed to optimize the weight vector, enhancing the robustness of range ambiguity resolution. Simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Shielded Stripline Bandpass Filters with Low Insertion Loss for 5G Applications
abstract: A novel method to design stripline filters with shielding structure is presented in this paper. By applying a shielded substrate integrated cavity a fully closed, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>-order filter with low loss is proposed for 5G N79 band. The shielding vias and copper layers form an enclosed cavity for the stripline filter composed of two gradient impedance resonators (GIR) and one stepped impedance resonator (SIR), which removes the radiation loss and improves the selectivity performance. A transmission zero is obtained by equating the gradient and low impedance parts of the GIR to an open-ended quarter wavelength stub. On the basis of this filter, a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> filter is designed by introducing a defected ground structure (DGS) and quarter wavelength stubs, which expands the passband and stopband. Both filters are fabricated and measured. The measured results are in good agreement with simulation, which validate the proposed design methodology. The minimum insertion loss is 0.46 dB and 0.25 dB for these two filters, respectively. The two filters are good candidates for 5G N79 applications.

articleTitle: Coexistence-Mode Composite Right/Left-Handed E-Plane Subatrate Integrate Waveguide Butler Matrix
abstract: The miniaturization design of beamforming network (BFN) is the key to improve the application value of the multibeam array antenna. This paper presents a miniaturized E-plane substrate integrate waveguide (SIW) Butler matrix (BM) based on the coexistence mode composite right/left-handed (Co-mode CRLH) substrate integrate waveguide (SIW) transmission lines technology. The interdigital slot (IDS) is introduced into the coupling region of the traditional E-plane couplers to construct the Co-mode CRLH transmission characteristics. By adjusting the size of the IDS, the phase constants of the TE10 mode and the quasi- TEM mode in the coupling region are controlled. By increasing the difference between two kinds of the phase constants, the length of the coupling region can be reduced, and the miniaturized E-plane BM is obtained. Compared with the traditional E-plane SIW BM, its longitudinal size is reduced by 22.1 %. The compact BM will be an attractive candidate for future millimeter wave (mm-wave) 5G terminal application.

articleTitle: Analysis FSS Absorber with Diversified Impedance for Broadband Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel resistively loaded double hexagonal loops circuit analog (CA) absorber is design and implementation. Especially the outer loops and the inner loops adopt different resistance values, thus realize broadband and strong absorption. The simulated results show that the proposed absorber provides a −10 dB absorption bandwidth of 4.6-16.3 GHz and −15 dB absorption bandwidth of 5.5-14.7 GHz. The working principle of the proposed absorber is revealed by the transmission-line equivalent circuit model. Dual-template silk-screen printing production is utilized to realized printing different resistance. The experimental results show good agreement with this simulated result. This method improved the feasibility of the design, make the resistively loaded FSS absorber more competitive in engineering application

articleTitle: Efficient Inverse Covariance Matrix Estimation for Low-Complexity Closed-Loop DPD Systems
abstract: This paper studies closed-loop digital predistortion systems, with special focus on linearization of mmW active antenna arrays. Considering the beam-dependent nonlinear dis - tortion and very high DPD processing rates, a modified self-orthogonalized (SO) learning solution is proposed, which is capable of reducing the computational complexity compared to other similar solutions, while at the same time obtaining a comparable linearization performance. The modified SO consits of a novel method for efficiently calculating the inverse of the input data covariance matrix. Thorough RF measurement results at 28 GHz band featuring a state-of-the-art 64 element active array and channel bandwidths up to 800 MHz, are reported A complexity analysis is also carried out which, together with the obtained results, allow to asses the performance-complexity trade-offs. Altogether, the results show that the proposed methods can facilitate efficient mmW active antenna array linearization.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band −200.2-dBc/Hz FoMT Low-Power Low-Phase-Noise LC-VCO IC with a Novel Feedback Circuit Using the Leakage Current
abstract: A Ku-band low-power low-phase-noise LC-VCO IC with a novel feedback circuit is presented in this paper. The novel feedback circuit controls a bias voltage to the VCO core circuit to reduce the dc power consumption and guarantees the robust start-up of the oscillation. The leakage current is utilized to drive the feedback circuit so that the dc power consumption in the feedback circuit is suppressed. The proposed Ku-band LC- VCO IC has exhibited a measured phase noise of −133.9 dBc/Hz, an FoM of −192.0 dBc/Hz, and an FoMT of −200.2 dBc/Hz under the maximum total power consumption of 2.98 mW.

articleTitle: A Cross Dipole Antenna Array in LTCC for Satellite Communication
abstract: A 4×4 antenna array operating in 26.5~31 GHz is designed with the low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology for satellite communication. The left-handed circular polarization is provided by cross dipoles fed with 90° phase difference for their two linear polarizations. For each channel including 1×4 subarray fed by a stripline structure, the in-band return loss is larger than 11 dB. The mutual coupling among four channels is lower than −16 dB. The peak realized gain of the 4×4 array is 14.7 dBi. A scanning angle of 100° is achieved with only 2.5 dB gain reduction and axial ratio less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: A Differentially-Fed Dielectric-loaded Antenna with Sidelobe Reduction Based on SISL Platform
abstract: A differentially-fed dielectric-loaded antenna with sidelobe suppression performance based on Substrate-Integrated Suspend Line (SISL) platform is proposed. The patch worked at TM03 is differentially fed and set on G5. A piece of high dielectric is loaded below the patch and then the current distribution of the patch is affected. The sidelobe of the antenna is reduced and Side-Lobe Level (SLL) of -5.4 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Direct-modulation Wireless Communication with Real-time Programmable Metasurface
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces make it possible to control electromagnetic (EM) wavefront in real time and allow to construct a new architecture for modern communication system. Here, we propose a wireless communication system based on binary amplitude-shift keying (BASK) by utilizing an L-band metasurface with two discrete states of reflection amplitude in far-field region. Experimental results demonstrate good performance of the proposed system, which may have potential in satellite communications.

articleTitle: Design of a miniaturized 2–18 GHz downconverter
abstract: Downconverter plays a unique role in radio frequency (RF) receiving systems, which converts the RF signal to the intermediate frequency (IF) signal. This paper proposes a design of a miniaturized 2–18 GHz downconverter with a 1 GHz processing bandwidth. The key electrical parameters of the designed downconverter are the noise figure (<8dB), the global dynamic range (>70dB), and the spurious signal level (<50dB). By using the integrated GaAs filter bank, the size of the RF circuit is increasingly miniaturized.

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Control for Digital Predistortion with Undersampled Feedback Signal
abstract: A novel undersampled feedback signal iterative learning control (US-ILC-DPD) technique is proposed to linearize RF power amplifiers (PAs). The proposed method combines the existing iterative learning control (ILC) with the undersampled processing. It can keep the good linearization performance and avoid using high speed ADCs, which are normally expensive and power costly. In addition, the advantages of ILC-DPD, such as low computational complexity and fast convergence rate, are all preserved in this approach. In linearization, an RFPA is excited by a 20-MHz LTE signal, which is sampled at 100, 25 and 12.5MSPS, respectively. Both the proposed approach and the conventional undersampled-DPD based on direct learning architecture (US-DLA) are validated. The experimental results show that, compared with the conventional US-DLA, the US-ILC-DPD has better robustness and linearization performance when the sampling rate is reduced. Meanwhile, the proposed US-ILC-DPD has much lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: A 40-GHz Power Amplifier With Output Power of 15.2 dBm in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: A millimeter wave (mm-Wave) power amplifier (PA) based on transformer matching network is presented in this paper. Two-stage common source (CS) differential structure PA is proposed which adopts cross-coupling capacitors to improve the stability and gain of the circuit, transformers are designed to simplify the design of impedance matching networks. Output matching is designed as a strongly coupled transformer to achieve low insertion loss, high output power and high efficiency, while the input and inter matching network is designed with low K (coupling coefficient) transformer to achieve better bandwidth. Designed and implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology with 1-V supply, the prototype delivers a saturated output power (Psat) of 15.2 dBm at 40 GHz, the maximum small-signal gain is 16.9 dB, and output IdB compression power (OPldB) is 12.41dBm with its corresponding power added efficiency (PAE) is 17.65%. The chip size is only 0.05 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding all DC pads.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Planar Coil Structures for Small-Size WPTs
abstract: A compact planar coil resonator-based wireless power transfer (WPT) system has been presented in this paper. The squared coil structure showed higher inductance and, hence, it was selected for the design of required resonators. The realized system has the small size of 40 × 40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The WPT was developed on Rogers RO3003 substrate. The operating frequency of the WPT is 433 MHz which corresponds to the practical industrial, scientific medical band. The practically realized WPT demonstrated the power transfer efficiency of 76% at the transmission distance of 22 mm.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Circuit Model to Interpret The Coupling Between FSS Layers
abstract: An equivalent circuit model to explain the coupling between FSS (frequency selective surface) is presented in this paper. The proposed method of establishing equivalent circuit models is suitable for the modeling of multi-layer FSSs and has higher rationality and accuracy than the most existing methods that do not consider coupling. Meanwhile, empirical equations are proposed to build the relationship between the coupling coefficients and the distance between layers. By using the empirical equations, the transmission/reflection coefficients of the FSS structure can be obtained directly without full-wave simulations. Simulations show that these equations are still valid when the size of the unit cells is changed.

articleTitle: A New Class of Symmetric Reflectionless Filter Topology And Its Applications to Coupled-Line Bandpass Filter Design
abstract: This paper presents a symmetric reflectionless filter topology that is capable of producing the canonical Butterworth responses with zero reflections at both ports. Straightforward design methods of a coupled-line bandpass filter using the newly synthesized filter topology are also given. Hence, a filter can be designed analytically without relying on a time-consuming numerical method. The measured frequency responses are in a good agreement with the synthesis.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Multifunctional Filtering Power Dividers
abstract: A direct synthesis design technique of multi-band multi-port filtering power dividers (FPDs) with arbitrary phase distribution is presented.
