After a set of complete closed-form analytical equations are established for direct synthesis design, the proposed method is intensively described to reveal its powerful capacity in design of a multifunctional FPD with any prespecified responses (e.g. any order, number of bands, number of ports, phase distribution etc.), high multi-band isolations and matching. To validate this design concept, a triple-band three-port FPD with phase difference of 90° has been implemented. The performance of the newly designed FPD is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Terahertz Monolithic Integrated Cavity Filter Based on SiC Substrate
abstract: In this paper, a terahertz integrated cavity band-pass filter (ICF) based on silicon carbide (SiC) has been proposed. The cascade triplet (CT) topology and over-moded cavity has been utilized to implement out-of-band suppression. Measurement showed that at the center frequency of 185GHz, insertion loss of the ICF is only 1.55dB, with a relative bandwidth of 9.7%. Two transmission zeros (TZs) has been produced, achieving the suppression of the upper side-band of higher than 40dB. Compared with a traditional cavity filter, the ICF is only one-thousandth of the volume with providing similar electric performance and better integration.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Circular Polarization Selective Surface with Stable Axial Ratio for Oblique Incidence
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized circular polarization selective surfaces (CPSS) for X-band applications. The design concept is based on modifications of the Pierrot cell, which divides a wire into two orthogonal parts and provides a strong coupling between the two orthogonal parts. The proposed CPSS is implemented by cross-inserting several identical printed circuit board (PCB) pieces, thus releasing difficulties in fabrication and assembly. Operation principle and design procedure are developed, then the optimal design parameters are found. As an example, a prototype of the designed CPSS working around 10 GHz is fabricated and measured. Measured results agree well with theoretical ones. Axial ratio and insertion loss smaller than 1 and 0.85 dB, respectively, at 10GHz up to 40° oblique incidence.

articleTitle: Single-layer Wideband Circuit Analog Absorber Combined Polarization Conversion
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band single-layer circuit analog (CA) absorber combined the absorption with other mechanisms is described. The design introduces the polarization-conversion (PC) into the resistor-loaded cross-dipole arrays. First, a single-layer wideband CA absorber with a metal backplate is designed. The inverted U as a polarization convertor is then used and optimized to improve the absorption bandwidth. It is shown through simulation and measurement that the proposed structure covers a dual band of 2.28 – 8.91 GHz and 13.65 – 18 GHz below −10 dB. It is worth mentioning that the structure can be used to diffuse the electromagnetic wave by rotating and combining the PC absorber.

articleTitle: A 77.2-dB SNDR SAR ADC With a Segmented Comparator Logic Based on Compensatory SA Latch for FIA
abstract: This paper presents a successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital convertor (ADC) dedicated to Internet of Things (IoT) applications. A segmented comparator logic with separated amplification phase and latch phase is proposed which enables sufficient amplification to achieve high resolution. Cooperating with the logic, a compensatory strong-arm (SA) latch is proposed for the floating invertor pre-amplifier (FIA), which guarantees both high gain and output stability of FIA. Implemented in 110nm CMOS technology, at a 1.5-V supply and 1 MS/s, the ADC achieves an SNDR of 77.2 dB and consumes 348 µw, resulting in a figure of merit (FoM) of 168.8 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-state Two-way Fano Switch in Plasmonic Metamaterials
abstract: Here a multi-state two-way Fano resonance switch in the plasmonic metamaterials has been proposed. The electrical Fano switch is composed of three concentric spoof localized surface plasmons (LSP) resonators. By adjusting the slit of the middle or inner spoof LSP resonator, four states of two kinds of Fano resonance modes could be supported. The devices could be applied in many applications such as plasmonic circuits, sensing or switching, and so on.

articleTitle: A Novel Circularly Polarized Antenna with Enhanced Axial-Ratio Bandwidth for Millimeter-wave Application
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The basic unit of the array is a novel CP ME-dipole. A differential feeding network composed of SICL is utilized for symmetric radiation pattern of the antenna. A new transition between SICL and rectangular waveguide is also designed for the feeding network. The simulated impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ 15 dB) and 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the antenna array are 16.5% and 15%, respectively. Besides, the simulated gain of the antenna array is around 12.5 dBi over the operating band.

articleTitle: A High-Gain and Broadband Sector-Shaped Double-Sided Printed Dipole Array Antenna for Ad-Hoc Network Nodes
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain double-sided printed dipole array antenna is designed for Ad-Hoc network nodes. By changing the shape of the oscillator element, it is designed as a novel exponential gradient sector structure to achieve good broadband characteristics. The antenna dipole radiator arm is symmetrically distributed on the upper and lower surfaces of the dielectric substrate. Taking the radiator element as the array element, an 8-element planar array with a reflecting plate is designed. Simulations show that the proposed printed dipole array antenna has a bandwidth of 400MHz for voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) < 2, which can meet the frequency band required by the Ad-Hoc network nodes. The experimental verification of the antenna shows that the working bandwidth is 480MHz, the relative bandwidth reaches 14.5%, and the experimental result is in good agreement with the simulation result. The maximum gain of the antenna at the frequency points of 3.3 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 3.7 GHz are all around 20.5dBi.

articleTitle: Compact Slot Antenna with Extended Bandwidth Integrated on Metal Box for 2.4 GHz IoT Applications
abstract: Two novel compact slot antennas for 2.4 GHz WLAN/Zigbee/Bluetooth applications have been proposed. The antennas are based on a metal hollow box, on which the slots are carved for radiation. These slots are meandered into compact shapes. To extend the bandwidth, each antenna has two slots, generating two resonant points that combine into a wide bandwidth. The prototypes are fabricated and tested, showing good radiation performance.

articleTitle: Development of A T/R Module for 5G Millimeter Wave Communication
abstract: This paper describes the development of a T/R module for mm-wave communication, working in 24.25-29.5 GHz. This T/R module's IF frequency is fixed at 3.5 GHz with 200 MHz bandwidth. The T/R module is designed with superheterodyne architecture, bases on commercially available RF surface mounted components from Analog Device, Inc. (ADI) and Qorvo. All of the chosen components are investigated separately, before the full integration on a multi-layer PCB consisted with RO4003C and FR4. The proposed design is planned to be used in a millimeter-wave MIMO communication system.

articleTitle: Bandpass Filter Inspired Filtering Patch Antenna
abstract: A planar filtering patch antenna inspired by BPF (bandpass filter) prototype is proposed in this paper. The antenna has a very simple structure, while realizing multifunctional operation, including directional radiation and filtering functions. The principle of replacing the LC resonator of BPF prototype with a patch resonator is illustrated. The newly obtained prototype is displayed in the physical form of a patch antenna fed by a differential coupled line. A microstrip-to-slotline transition is introduced to generate the differential signal. As a result, the proposed antenna achieves good filtering response with two radiation nulls on the two sides of the passband. The measured results agree well with simulation.

articleTitle: A 6–18 GHz Multifunction Heterodyne RF Transceiver Module on LTCC with SAW and BAW Bandpass Filters
abstract: This paper proposes a 6–18 GHz LTCC multifunction heterodyne transceiver architecture. To meet the multifunctional application and improve the rejection of spurious signals, four types of micro-acoustic bandpass filter (BPF) chips including the narrowband surface acoustic wave (SAW) filter, the wideband SAW filter and the C-band bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filter are designed, fabricated and integrated into the transmit (TX) and receive (RX) chains. The proposed transceiver module has been fabricated by the low temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) process. The transceiver module has a compact size of 22×15×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, including four independent frequency conversion channels with a RX gain of more than 20 dB and a TX output power of more than 11 dBm.

articleTitle: A Hybrid SAW-Resonator/Lumped-Element Dual-Band Bandstop Filter with Continuously Tunable Bandwidths
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid SAW-resonator/lumped-element dual-band bandstop filter with continuously tunable bandwidths (BWs) is reported. It is based on hybrid-technology design approach in which N identical dual-resonance filter cells-shaped by two SAW resonators, one coupling capacitor, two inductors and two varactors-are cascaded in series by N-l transmission lines Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. In this manner, two stopband notches with enhanced fractional bandwidths (FBWs) which are larger than the electromechanical coupling coefficient (k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t<sup>2</sup></sub>) can be achieved. The continuously variable BWs are realized by adjusting the bias voltages of varactor diodes. For practical validation, a prototype using commercially-available one-port SAW resonators and chip LE components is designed, built and tested. It exhibits two stop-bands centered at 868.7 and 916.7 MHz that respectively expose continuous BW tuning between 1.06-3.27 k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t<sup>2</sup></sub> and 0.89-2.62 k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t<sup>2</sup></sub>.

articleTitle: Design of broadband high-power one-to-three power divider based on LTCC
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband one-to-three power divider based on a lumped element circuit structure. Using the advantages of the LTCC multilayer structure, the capacitor and inductance model is loaded inside it to replace the traditional 1/4 impedance matching line, which realizes the miniaturization of the power divider. The overall size of the structure is 3.3 mm × 3.04 mm × 0.96 mm. And by loading a broadband matching network at the input, the bandwidth of the power splitter is greatly expanded. The power divider is simulated and analyzed by HFSS simulation software. The center frequency of the power divider in this design is 2.4 GHz, the relative bandwidth reaches 41 % (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -20 dB), the insertion loss is less than -1 dB, the standing wave ratio is less than 1.2, and the isolation is less than -20 dB, power capacity greater than 8W, this structure has excellent performance and stable structure. It has good application prospects in mobile communication WiFi transceiver, 5G micro base station and other scenarios.

articleTitle: A 310-GHz Area and Power Efficient Oscillator in 65-nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a compact CMOS signal source for the large-scale THz array with high output power and DC-to-RF efficiency. The proposed single harmonic THz VCO utilizes a high-order LC tank to resonate out the parasitic capacitors distributedly, and generate the second harmonic signal efficiently. The 310-GHz 65-nm bulk CMOS prototype in post-layout simulation achieves a high output power of 2.3-dBm and 3.8% effi-ciencv in a compact 0.01-mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area.

articleTitle: Mechanically Switchable Geometry Phase Metasurfaces For Circular Polarization Antenna Transmission- and Reflection-Wavefront Manipulations
abstract: In this study, a novel switchable full-space ABA meta-atom with two modified H-shaped structures combined with frequency selective surface (FSS) units was proposed. We presented a novel method for the design, fabrication, and characterization of switchable metasurfaces, whose radiation direction of modulated circular polarized waves can be easily changed. The novel efficient ABA meta-atom have transmission amplitude of >0.96, reflection amplitude of >0.98, and 2π phase control. A mechanically switchable, high-gain antenna based on the metasurfaces was then developed to validate the proposed design. The antenna functioned as a transmitarray and reflectarray antenna at approximately 10 GHz with 19.1 and 19.5 dBic, respectively, and aperture efficiency of 39% and 42%, respectively. Experimental results of the assembled switchable antenna were in good agreement with the simulated results. The proposed method is promising in many full-space symmetry and chirality devices such as orbital angular momentum generators and holograms.

articleTitle: Research on Frequency Multiplier Behavioral Model Based on K-parameter
abstract: To extract the behavioral model of frequency multiplier, the theory and method of K-parameter are proposed. A terahertz frequency tripler circuit is used to extract the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-parameter model. When a 50 Ω load is connected at the output port, the model can accurately characterize the amplitude and phase of the input and output products of the tripler. When the input frequency is interpolated, the simulation accuracy of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-parameter model is equivalent to that of the X-parameter model, and it can also characterize the mixer's characteristics under a certain harmonic impedance mismatch state.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband VCO Using Digitally Controlled Varactor Arrays in 40-nm CMOS Technology
abstract: The paper presents an ultra-wideband and low phase-noise voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) for 5G applications. To tackle the bandwidth limitation and lossy issue induced by commonly used switched capacitor banks for frequency tuning, the novel method of using digitally controlled varactor arrays is proposed and investigated. Improved phase noise, tuning range, and reduced power consumption are obtained from theoretical analysis and circuit simulations. To validate the design theory, a X-band VCO with 4-bit varactor array is designed and implemented in a 40-nm CMOS technology. The full-wave electromagnetic assisted post-layout simulations show the VCO features a broad tuning range of 8.86-13.4GHz (41%) with only 6 mW DC power consumption from a 1.1V supply. The FoM/FoMT of -185/-197 dBc/Hz are among the state-of-the-art designs.

articleTitle: A Low-profile Wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Tightly Coupled Dipole Array Antenna
abstract: A low-profile wideband array antenna with wide-angle scanning is presented. The proposed antenna is based on tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) backed with metal ground plane. A parasitic strip and an integrated Marchand balun are incorporated within each element to further broaden the bandwidth. A metasurface layer is utilized as wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) superstrate of the array to enhance its scanning performance. The simulated results of the designed infinite array model show that it can achieve 8.06:1 bandwidth (1.87-15.08 GHz for VSWR < 3) for boresight radiation. Maximum angle of 75° and 65° can be obtained for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-planes scanning cases, respectively, although 45° is observed for scanning in the H-plane. A finite array with 10×10 elements is demonstrated with simulation results of radiation performance. The profile of the presented array above ground plane is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.08\lambda_{l}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{l}$</tex> is the wavelength in open space at the lowest operating frequency.

articleTitle: An Accurate and Fast Method to Determine Antenna Directivity in Near-field Scanning Measurement
abstract: Near-filed (NF) scanning measurement is an effective way to evaluate the antenna radiation characteristics, among which antenna directivity is an important parameter for radar systems. In this paper, an accurate and fast method is proposed to determine the antenna directivity based on NF scanning measurement. The antenna far-field (FF) patterns are firstly produced by extrapolating the planar NF data obtained in NF scanning, then the antenna directivity can be estimated using the pattern integral method. Different from the existing methods, an integral transformation method is proposed to calculate the pattern integral, which deals with the FF responses in the wavenumber domain directly, avoiding the complex interpolation operation in angle domain. The proposed method is verified with both simulated data and experimental data. The results indicate that the proposed method can significantly promote the computation efficiency and estimation accuracy, which is superior to the existing methods.

articleTitle: Propagation Measurement System at 220 GHz
abstract: In this paper, a long-distance propagation measurement system at 220 GHz is proposed. In order to tackle the challenge of long-distance (i.e., 2.5 km) terahertz propagation, TX/RX RF -fronts, high-gain antennas, and intermediate-frequency (IF)/ digital signal processing platform are all deliberately designed and utilized to achieve sufficient link-budget margin. As compared with other existing above-100 GHz measurement solutions, the proposed system can complete the propagation measurement with longer distance. To validate the proposed system, related measurements are carried out to confirm the performance, including the test of the transmitted power, noise figure/gain of RX link, etc. To measure the propagation loss for the long-distance scenario, out-door experiments are performed, whose results is compared with the predicted results based on international telecommunication union (ITU) model. Loss gap is observed between these two results. Therefore, in order to obtain accurate prediction on the terahertz-wave propagation loss, it is highly necessary to make revision on the traditional ITU model. The proposed measurement system would make contributions for such revision.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multilayer Lossy FSS Based Broadband Absorber
abstract: Combined with the unique dispersion characteristics of the resistive film, a multilayer broadband lossy FSS absorber containing three basic topological types is proposed in this paper. The relative bandwidth is fL/fH 151.8% (1.6-11.7 GHz) with the thickness of 33 mm. Each layer is printed by resistive ink with square resistance of 50 Ohm/sq. The measurement is consistent with the simulation, which prove the validity of the design.

articleTitle: Lie Detection Based on a DIFCW Radar with Machine Learning
abstract: Lying is a common behavior that humans deceive and mislead others by concealing plots, false statements, and distorting facts which is important for intelligence service, bank, and justice department. In this paper, a system based on a DIFCW radar with machine learning is presented to perform polygraph. The radar is utilized to achieve non-contact measurement of heartbeat and respiratory signals. Based on the two signals, several features are extracted. And a model is trained through machine learning to determine whether the subject lie. In the experiment, a database of 11 males and 10 females with 435 lies and 562 truths are established. The accuracy rate of heartbeat and respiratory polygraph detection attach to 63.2% and 61.5%.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Filtering Devices Based on Multi-Mode Dielectric Resonators
abstract: This paper presents three filtering devices using high-Q quad-mode dielectric resonator (DR) including a frequency-agile dual-band balanced filter, a dual-band diplexer and a balun diplexer. Based on the field distribution, the quad-mode excitations and differential-mode (DM) operations are both revealed only using straight probes. According to the quad-mode orthogonality, the independent controls and individual transmissions of the multiple modes are investigated. Then the independently tunable passbands and high isolation between different channels are both realized. For verification, the first two devices are both designed and fabricated. By sharing the quad-mode DR, the compact sizes are ensured. The measured result agrees well with the simulated one, supporting the proposed method in miniaturized multi-band DR designs.

articleTitle: Range Ambiguous Clutter Rank Analysis in FDA-MIMO Radar
abstract: In recent years, frequency diverse array (FDA) with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique, which is referred to as FDA-MIMO radar, has attracted extensive attentions due to its outstanding advantages of introducing additional controllable degrees-of-freedom (DOFs) in range dimension. For FDA-MIMO radar mounted on a moving platform, one big concern is clutter rank. This paper derives the analytical expression of clutter rank in FDA-MIMO radar with range ambiguity. The clutter rank is studied based on subspace transformation and the correlation of vectors in the transformed subspace is explored. Then the maximum resolvable number of range ambiguity can be determined. Simulation results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Continuous Scanning Leaky-wave Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
abstract: A continuous scanning leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is proposed using a patch array fed by planar spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP). The LWA is capable of scanning its beam from backward to the forward direction. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the antenna is 6.5 to 10GHz. It is shown that the scanning angle can reach 55 degrees with an average gain level of 9.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of an X/Ku band overmoded coaxial waveguide diplexer for high power microwaves
abstract: In this paper, we present an overmoded coaxial waveguide diplexer at X/Ku band for high power microwaves. The design details and diplexing mechanism have been investigated. An overmoded filter based on coaxial corrugated waveguide is proposed as a band pass filter, which operates at TEM mode. To suppress excited TMon modes and keep fundamental TEM mode, the filter is optimized and designed. The designed filter possesses a transmission efficiency over 99% from 9.23GHz to 9.47GHz, while reflection efficiency is over 99% from 9.35GHz to 9.65GHz. A concentric waveguide with 22 coupling holes is designed as an injection structure to diplex Ku band microwaves to the overmoded coaxial waveguide and at the same time stop the X band microwaves. Hence, the diplexing manifold can combine X band and Ku band microwaves into the common waveguide. According to the simulation results, the power handling capacity of the designed diplexer is at giga-watt level, and its transmission efficiency is over 99%.

articleTitle: Beam-scanning circularly polarized antenna array based on Liquid Crystal
abstract: A circularly polarized(CP) antenna array with the capability of beam-scanning based on liquid crystal(LC) is proposed. TUD-649 LC is adopted to realize beam steering by controlling the permittivity of LC. Circular polarization is obtained using two orthogonal slots. The radiation array is fed by four-port power dividers. The peak gain of the antenna is 10.5 dBi. The scanning angles from -20° to 20° are achieved at 12.6GHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Microstrip/Fabry-Perot Resonator Cavity Antenna with Large Frequency Ratio
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid antenna with large frequency ratio is proposed. The frequency ratio of the two operating bands reaches 7.3. A meshed mirostrip patch antenna contributes to the radiation at microwave band. However, the radiation at millimeter wave comes from a Fabry-Perot resonator cavity antenna. These two antennas share one single aperture, which realizes structure reuse. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB) reaches 5% and 6.5% at lower band and higher band, respectively. The peak gains are 8.0 dBi and 12.82 dBi at 3.7 GHz and 27.1 GHz, respectively. The total size of the proposed antenna is only 40mm× 40mm× 5. 3mm. The proposed antenna shows potential applications on the base station of a 5G communication system.

articleTitle: A Wide-Beam 3D-Fractal Hilbert GNSS Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a wide-beam 3D-fractal Hilbert GNSS antenna in the RDSS-S band. The proposed antenna consists of a novel radiator with four two-order 3D-fractal Hilbert curve radiating arms, and the corresponding feeding circuit. The beamwidth, with the gain greater than 0dB of the antenna, is 148° (Phi=0°) and 138° (Phi=90°). The size of the antenna is 30mm×30mm×12mm. In addition, the model of the 3D-fractal Hilbert curve and a prototype of the two-order RDSS-S antenna were manufactured by 3D printing. Simulated and measured results show that the proposed wide-beam 3D-Fractal Hilbert antenna is very suitable for GNSS.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Dual-Band Bandpass-to-Bandstop Filter Using SAW Resonators and Lumped Elements
abstract: The RF design of a dual-band bandpass-to-bandstop filter that employs surface-acoustic-wave (SAW) resonators is reported. It is based on SAW resonators combined with lumped elements and a RF signal path controlled by PIN diode. The bandpass-to-bandstop (BP-to-BS) transformation is realized by adj usting the DC bias voltage of PIN diode and the value of variable capacitor. In this way, the filter features narrow bandwidths and analog transmission zeros tuning in bandpass-mode and enhanced fractional bandwidths (FBWs) in bandstop-mode. The proposed concept is experimentally verified by a second-order manufactured filter with two bands centered at 868.7 and 916.7 MHz. It exhibits a bandpass-mode with FBWs of 0.44, 0.61k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t<sup>2</sup></sub>, insertion loss of 2.80, 1.91 dB and a bandstop-mode with FBWs of 1.50, 1.12k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t<sup>2</sup></sub>, stopband isolation of 30.7,28 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized High Isolation 5G Band Coupler Based on LTCC
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized 5G band 20dB coupler based on low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) materials, which makes full use of the characteristics of LTCC that can be stacked in multiple layers, and realizes the overall miniaturization, more compact structure, and the coupling Load the short-circuit branch of the isolation section to improve the isolation to 42 dB. The four ports are placed in a “cross” shape, which is convenient for later connection with filters and power splitters to achieve more application scenarios. This structure is between 4.4 GHz and 5 GHz to achieve the insertion loss of 0.13 dB. The complete structure size is 3.5 mm × 2.3 mm × 0.96 mm. It works in the sub6 frequency band of 5G, which will have a lot of room for mobile communication.

articleTitle: SAR Target Detection Based on NCM-1K Clustering
abstract: In training-free Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target detection, it is difficult to distinguish targets and non-targets accurately. To solve the problem, a new improved NCM clustering method with one clustering center (K=1), as called NCM-1K clustering method, is proposed in this paper. The principle of NCM-1K is to divide the potential target areas into target areas and non-target areas according to the Polar Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (PSIFT) descriptor. The proposed NCM-1K clustering method can realize the SAR target detection with free-training. Experimental results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circularly-Polarized Waveguide Slot Cavity Array
abstract: This paper presents a new broadband circularly-polarized antenna array. The principle of circularly-polarized radiation is realized by orthogonal waveguide slots with a 90° spatial phase delay based on the special structure of the L-shaped waveguide. The simulation results show that it achieves a relative impedance bandwidth (VSWR 2) of 27.1 %, covering a frequency range from 18.9 GHz to 24.8 GHz, a relative circularly-polarized bandwidth (axial ratio ≤ 3 dB) of 17.3 %, and an aperture efficiency of 79.7 ~ 90.9%. At the same time, its full-metal structure and two-dimensional scanning capability of ±15° are very suitable for harsh space environment applications.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Aperiodic Bragg Reflector-Inspired Filters with Compact Size for High-Power Applications
abstract: The design and optimization of a high-power filter based on the Bragg reflector is presented in this paper. Theoretical analysis of the aperiodic Bragg reflector reveals that, by replacing the periodic cylindrically symmetric corrugations (CSCs) into random ones, required filtering performance may be realized in a designated frequency band. An improved optimization strategy based on covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) is introduced to optimize CSCs for the filter design. Besides, in order to maximize the power capacity and maintain the designed accuracy, the chamfering technique is presented and integrated into the optimization. An optimized geometry, which respectively exhibit the band-pass response with central frequencies of 9.3GHz and ±100MHz bandwidth, is fabricated and measured. Measured results validate the design and optimization with the required operation band, out-of-band suppression ratio and input power handling capability. The experiment results show that HPM beams are successfully operated at 2GW with pulse width of 105 ns.

articleTitle: A Novel Multibeam Slot Array Antenna Based on Parabolic Lens BFN for Mass Production
abstract: In this letter, a simple SIW multibeam antenna on the ground of parabolical lens beam-Forming network is put forward for mobile satellite communications. The presented antenna is consisted of a port part (Rogers RT/duroid 5880) as well as an antenna part (Rogers RT/duroid 6002). By manufacturing the antenna part via substrates of different dielectric constant, whereas maintained the port deck, flexible beam tunability is implemented in this multibeam antenna. The gain of the antenna up to 14.5 dBi within 27 GHz~ 28 GHz after experimental verification. Wide scan angle of beams varying from -59° to 62° is also observed. This antenna characterized better property and simpler architecture while compared with others. The operation principle, design process, and performance of the proposed antenna are expounded sequentially.

articleTitle: A Wideband Noise-Cancelling Balun Low Noise Amplifier with Self-Adaptive Calibration for Low Power Application
abstract: A wideband noise-cancelling balun low noise amplifier (LNA) with process, supply voltage and temperature (PVT) calibration for low power application is presented in the paper. The proposed LNA consists of the matching amplifier and the voltage sensing amplifier with feedback resistor to achieve noise cancelling and also offers differential outputs. To stabilize DC-operation point and avoid output imbalance of the proposed LNA, a DC tracking loop is utilized by adjusting the supply voltage of the LNA. The proposed LNA is implemented in a 40 nm CMOS process, and occupies 0.101 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip area. Measurement results show that it achieves maximum voltage gain of 23.2 dB, minimum NF of 5.9 dB, input referred third-order intercept point (IIP3) higher than -6 dBm, and can operate from 1.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz with input return loss of less than -8 dB, while it draws 1.9 mA from 1.1 V voltage supply.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reflectarray Based on Polarization Rotating Unit Cells
abstract: We present a new wideband single-layer reflectarray based on polarization rotating (PR) unit cells. These PR unit cells convert a linearly polarized incident electromagnetic wave to an orthogonal polarization upon reflection wave. Each unit cell consists of a pair of L-shaped patches and a metallic strip tilted at 45° from the x-axis in the xy plane. By adjusting the dimension of this unit cell, a pair of 90° phase difference unit cells were achieved. And we used these two unit cells and their mirror images to achieve a 2 bit phase shifter, which provides a phase shift of 0°/90°/180°/270° from 11 GHz to 17 GHz. Based on the proposed element, a wideband reflectarray is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the reflectarray's maximum gain is 25.6 dBi, with a 1 dB gain bandwidth of 30.4 % and an aperture efficiency of 35%, which agree well with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna with Multidirctional Beam for 5G Microbase Stations
abstract: A base station antenna capable of multidirectional pattern reconfiguration is presented. The antenna structure consists of a driven base station antenna and two parasitic dipoles that act either as reflector(s) or director(s) depending on the switching arrangement. Beam reconfiguration is achieved by using two pin diode switches which affect the current distribution of the parasitic dipole. The proposed antenna achieves twelve distinguished main beam angular positions. The measured common bandwidth of the nine modes is 3.4-3.8 GHz which covers 5G, and the isolations between two ports in all the modes are higher than 15 dB. The proposed antenna could be a suitable candidate for 5G microbase stations.

articleTitle: Alternating Iteration Algorithm for Rectangular Waveguide Based Permittivity Measurement
abstract: To mitigate the two limitations existing in the conventional procedures of Nicolson-Ross- Weir (NRW) method, namely thickness resonance and multi-value problems, an alternating iteration algorithm is proposed for accurately retrieving the complex permittivity of non-magnetic materials based on rectangular waveguide measurements. The mechanism for the generating of the two limitations are reviewed and explained with the detailed procedures. Then, two different types of formulas are combined together for alternately iterative calculation, effectively eliminating two limitations simultaneously. The proposed algorithm has been described, and verified with numerous simulations as well as experiments, exhibiting robustness and high accuracy.
